NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING AND AGENDA
NAVAJO COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS
Tuesday, July 18, 2023
ONE OR MORE SUPERVISORS MAY ATTEND VIA VIDEO AND/OR TELEPHONICALLY 
The Navajo County Board of Supervisors will hold a meeting open to the public on Tuesday, July 18, 2023, in the Supervisors’
Chamber in the Navajo County Governmental Complex, 100 East Code Talkers Drive, Holbrook, Arizona. The Board may vote to
meet in a closed executive session to discuss certain matters and for legal advice on any item as indicated on the following
agenda, pursuant to A.R.S. § 38-431.03(A) (3). 
The Navajo County Board of Supervisors finds that it is in the best interest of the community to conduct this public meeting using
a hybrid method in order to serve the public interest. 
Join Zoom Meeting, click here: https://us06web.zoom.us/j/87692173340?pwd=WDU3WWhlZFcxd1JqN1BzYXI1dUdpZz09 
 
Call In Number: 1-253-215-8782 OR 1-346-248-7799 (You may use either teleconference number)
Meeting ID: 876 9217 3340
Passcode: 271616
Persons with disabilities who need accommodation to attend or participate in the meeting may contact the Clerk of the Board’s
office at (928) 524-4053; at least 48 hours prior to the meeting, so an accommodation can be arranged.
Items on the agenda may be considered out of order at the Chairman’s discretion. A copy of the agenda background material
provided to the Board, except items to be considered in executive session, is available for public inspection at Navajo County
website, www.navajocountyaz.gov
“NOTICE TO PARENTS AND LEGAL GUARDIANS: Parents and legal guardians have the right to consent before Navajo County makes a video
or voice recording of a minor child, pursuant to A.R.S. § 1-602(A)(9). The Navajo County Board of Supervisors regular meetings are recorded and
may be viewed on Navajo County’s website, and social media pages. If you permit your child to attend/participate in a televised Navajo County
Board of Supervisors meeting, a recording will be made, and your child’s picture may be posted on Navajo County’s social media pages. You may
exercise your right not to consent by not allowing your child to attend/participate in the meeting.” 
9:00 a.m. Call To Order: Invocation and Pledge of Allegiance
           
1. CALL TO THE PUBLIC: Individuals may address the Board on any relevant issue for up
to 3 minutes. At the close of the call to the public, Board members may not respond to any
comments but may respond to criticism, ask staff to review a matter or ask that a matter be
placed on a future agenda.
 
 
2. CONSENT AGENDA: These items are considered to be routine or administrative in nature
and will be approved in a single motion. A Board member may request for any item to be
removed from the consent agenda and considered on the regular agenda:
 
 
a. Minutes: June 20, 2023, Special Meeting; June 20, 2023, Executive Session; June 26, 2023,
Special Meeting; June 26, 2023, Executive Session; June 27, 2023, Regular Meeting; June
27, 2023, Executive Session; June 28, 2023, Special Meeting, and July 11, 2023, Special
Meeting
 
 
b. Warrant & Voucher Report over $1000, June 2023

<!-- page 2 -->
c. Constable Reports: Holbrook Precinct #1, April 2023, May 2023, June 2023; Snowflake
Precinct #3, June 2023; Show Low Precinct #5, June 2023; and Pinetop-Lakeside Precinct
#6, June 2023
 
 
d. Sympathy Letters: Ciera Hensley (Health District), Jeffery Brown (Jail Operations), and
Kari Lopez (Treasurer)
 
 
e. Certificate of Removal and Abatement Purging Record of Tax, Penalty and Interest on
Personal Property Taxes, pursuant to A.R.S. §42-19118 and 42-18353
 
 
f. Extension Letter acknowledgment for Contract B20-01-030 Bank Services Agreement with
Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. which includes Exhibit A-Pricing Schedule (reverts back to the
original pricing), Exhibit B-Contract and Eligibility for Cooperative Purchasing Form,
Exhibit C-Bank Servicing Agreement and Exhibit D-Wells Fargo Bank N.A.'s Response to
Request for Proposal for Bank Servicing Agreement (including Appendix)
 
 
g. FY24 ACJC Victims' Compensation Grant #VC-24-010 for salary and ERE for
administering the Victim Compensation program as well as provides benefits for victims of
crime
 
 
h. Intergovernmental Agreement for Provision of Services by the Arizona Secretary of State
and Navajo County
 
 
i. Contracts signed by County Manager pursuant to Board of Supervisors Resolution: Contract
with Jay Valenzuela for the Northern Arizona Law Enforcement Training Academy as a
Recruit Training Officer and Contract for Professional Services with HDR Engineering, Inc.
for Engineering Consultant, Contract No. B23-02-015, Task 2 Modernization of
Engineering Design Guideline and Standard Details Project
 
 
j. Amendment to the ground lease agreement with Cellular One  
 
3. EMPLOYEE RECOGNITION:  
 
a. Navajo County recognizes the following employees for their excellence in personal
performance far exceeding organization expectations for the month of June: Jennifer
Ober (Public Works), Octavia Thompson (Health District), Nikki Olson (Health District),
and Colleen Smith (BOS/Administration)
 
Presented By: Lea Petersen
 
4. ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES:  
 
a. Personnel Service Awards: Congratulations to the following employees for their continued
service to Navajo County: Brent Hartman (Sheriff) 5; Clayton Yazzie (Jail Operations) 5; 
Donald Perkins (Public Works) 5; Jason Cash (Probation) 15; Salli O'Hair (Sheriff) 25;
and Eileen Rogers (Public Fiduciary) 30.
 
Presented By: Eric Scott

<!-- page 3 -->
b. Presentation by Glenn Kephart of the Dr. Seuss Award  
Presented By: Glenn Kephart
 
5. BOARD OF SUPERVISORS:  
 
a. Presentation to Brad Carlyon on receiving the Michael C. Cudahy Criminal Justice Award
from the State Bar of Arizona
 
Presented By: Glenn Kephart/Board of Supervisors
 
b. Presentation of the activities of the County Supervisors Association for FY2022-23.  
Presented By: Craig Sullivan, CSA Executive Director/CSA President Jason Whiting
 
c. PUBLIC HEARING: Consideration and Adoption of Resolution Number 22-23,
deannexing territory from the Town of Pinetop-Lakeside and annexing the same territory to
the City of Show Low.
 
Presented By: Jason Moore
 
d. PUBLIC HEARING: Consideration of a Liquor License from Maria Suarez for Casa
Ramos, for a 012 Restaurant license located at 1849 Highway 260, Heber, AZ.
 
Presented By: Leah Thomas
 
6. NAVAJO COUNTY PUBLIC HEALTH SERVICES DISTRICT: Board of Directors
Session: 
 
 
a. CONSENT AGENDA: The following item(s) are considered to be of a routine or
administrative in nature and will be approved as a group unless a member of the Board
wishes to discuss a particular item: 
 
 
1. Amendment Number 3 to the Intergovernmental Agreement, Contract #CTR055412, for
Healthy People Healthy Communities, between the Arizona Department of Health Services
and Navajo County Public Health Services District
 
 
2. Renewal of Intergovernmental Agreement, Tuberculosis Control Contract #CTR066508,
Program through Arizona Department of Health Services (ADHS) with Navajo County
Public Health (NCPHSD)
 
 
3. Renewal of Tuberculosis Contract between White Mountain Radiology and Navajo County
Public Health Services District to provide x-ray services
 
 
4. Renewal of the State Government agreement, GRA-STATE-24-1245-01, Child Care Health
Consultation strategy with First Things First, for fiscal year 2024, July, 1 2023, to June 30,
2024

<!-- page 4 -->
5. Memorandum of Agreement between Navajo County and FEMA regarding the continued
use of the Integrated Public Alert and Warning System
 
 
b. REGULAR AGENDA:  
 
1. Consideration and approval to implement a fee for service for CPR and First Aid
certification and be recognized as a Training Center.
 
Presented By: Janelle Linn & Amy Stradling
 
2. Consideration for approval  of an amendment to the existing Intergovernmental Agreement
between Coconino County Public Health Services District and Navajo County Public Health
Services District for the continued use of the Coconino Public Health Medical Consultant /
Alternative Medical Examiner Services, including a 4% increase for services rendered.
 
Presented By: Rhonda Krouse
 
7. PUBLIC WORKS:  
 
a. Consideration of Resolution Number 23-2023, granting a Right-of-Way Abandonment of
an un-named partial cul-de-sac adjacent to lots 74, 75, & 76 recorded in plat book 5 page 45. 
 
Presented By: Madhav Mundle
 
b. Consideration of Task Agreement Number 14 to the Memorandum of Agreement No.
20-049 with the Hopi Tribe Department of Transportation. 
 
Presented By: Madhav Mundle
 
c. Consideration of Task Agreement Number 34 to the Intergovernmental Agreement between
the Bureau of Indian Affairs-Navajo Region and Navajo County that authorizes funding
assistance to provide gravel material on BIA Route 8065 within the Central Agency. 
 
Presented By: Madhav Mundle
 
d. Consideration of accepting a grant award in the amount of $261,000 from FY2022
Rebuilding American Infrastructure with Sustainability and Equity (RAISE) Grant Program
with $29,000 local match and authorizing staff to conduct the Southern Navajo County
Regional Multimodal Planning Study in compliance with the grant's terms and conditions.
 
Presented By: Madhav Mundle & Ken Maruyama
 
e. PLANNING & DEVELOPMENT:  
 
1. PUBLIC HEARING: Consideration and possible adoption of Resolution Number
24-2023, approving/denying a Zone Change from A-General to R-3 to allow for a 17-space
manufactured home park in Lakeside on a 3.48-acre portion of APN# 212-26-119A,
212-26-119C, 212-26-119D, and 212-26-119E.
 
Presented By: Sondra Starke
 
2. PUBLIC HEARING: Consideration and possible adoption of Resolution Number

<!-- page 5 -->
2. PUBLIC HEARING: Consideration and possible adoption of Resolution Number
25-2023, approving/denying a Special Use Permit to allow for a 17-space manufactured
home park in Lakeside on a 3.48-acre portion of APN# 212-26-119A, 212-26-119C,
212-26-119D, and 212-26-119E.
 
Presented By: Sondra Starke
 
3. PUBLIC HEARING: Consideration and possible adoption of Resolution Number
26-2023, approving/denying a Special Use Permit to allow for the construction of a
two-phased project, which consists of a Manufactured Home Park and fourplex on a vacant,
2.83-acre parcel, in the Lakeside area, APN# 212-26-082N, Township 09 North, Range 22
East, Section 24 of the Gila and Salt River Base and Meridian.
 
Presented By: Cody Cooper
 
4. PUBLIC HEARING: Consideration and possible adoption of Resolution Number
27-2023, approving/denying a Special Use Permit to allow for the construction of a 110'
monopine wireless communication tower and associated facility on a vacant, 7.63-acre
parcel, in the Show Low area, APN# 210-01-009F, Township 10 North, Range 22 East,
Section 33 of the Gila and Salt River Base and Meridian.
 
Presented By: Cody Cooper
 
f. VICTORY HEIGHTS ROAD MAINTENANCE DISTRICT: Board of Directors
Session:
 
 
1. CONSENT AGENDA: The following item(s) are considered to be of a routine or
administrative in nature and will be approved as a group unless a member of the Board
wishes to discuss a particular item: 
 
 
a. Amendment Number 2 to the Victory Heights Road Maintenance District, Contract
#B21-07-022 extending the contract for one additional year (September 14, 2023, to
September 13, 2024) with no price increase
 
 
8. BOARD OF SUPERVISORS:  
 
a. Presentation to outgoing County Manager, Glenn Kephart  
Presented By: Board of Supervisors/Staff
 
9. COUNTY BUSINESS UPDATE: Report from County Manager, County Attorney and
Board members.
 
 
 
10. ADJOURN  
 
11. GLENN KEPHART RETIREMENT CELEBRATION: Pursuant to ARS § 38-431.02

<!-- page 6 -->
11. GLENN KEPHART RETIREMENT CELEBRATION: Pursuant to ARS § 38-431.02
and ARS § 38-431 (3), notice is hereby given to the members of the Navajo County Board
of Supervisors and to the General Public that a quorum of the Board of Supervisors may be
present for a Retirement Celebration in honor of Glenn Kephart in the Code Talkers
Conference Room, at 100 East Code Talkers Drive in Holbrook, Arizona where no official
action will be taken. 
 
 
Dated: July 14, 2023 NAVAJO COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS 
Posted: 10:50 a.m. By: MWB                         
Melissa W. Buckley - Clerk of the Board

Board of Supervisors Regular 2. g.        
Meeting Date: 07/18/2023  
Title: FY24 ACJC Victims' Compensation Grant
Submitted For: Brad Carlyon, County Attorney  Submitted By: Lynda Young, Office
Manager
Department: County Attorney
Motion before the Board:
FY24 ACJC Victims' Compensation Grant #VC-24-010 for salary and ERE for administering
the Victim Compensation program as well as provides benefits for victims of crime
Background:
The victim compensation program provides financial assistance to victims of crime or others
who may have experienced a financial loss as a direct result of a crime. The program covers
expenses of physical harm, mental distress, and economic loss directly resulting from
victimization. Funds from this grant provide salary and ERE for administering the
Compensation program as well as provides benefits for victims of crime.
Fiscal Impact
Fiscal Year: FY24
Budgeted Y/N: Y
Amount Requested: 134862.00
Fiscal Impact:
Grant is $134,862.00 with no match requirement.

GRANTEE;
NOW, THEREFORE, it is agreed between the parties as follows:
1. This Agreement will commence on July 01, 2023 and terminate on June 30, 2024. This Agreement expires
at the end of the award period unless prior written approval for an extension has been obtained from the
COMMISSION. A request for an extension must be received by the COMMISSION sixty (60) days prior to the end
of the award period. The COMMISSION in its sole discretion may approve an extension that furthers the goals
and objectives of the program and shall determine the length of any extension.
2. GRANTEE agrees that grant funds will be used in accordance with applicable program rules, guidelines and
special conditions.
3. The COMMISSION will monitor GRANTEE performance against program goals and performance standards
and
those outlined in the grant application. Substandard performance as determined by the COMMISSION will
constitute noncompliance with this Agreement. If the COMMISSION finds noncompliance, the GRANTEE will
receive a written notice which identifies the area of noncompliance, and the appropriate corrective action to be
taken. If the GRANTEE does not respond within thirty (30) calendar days to this notice, and does not provide
sufficient information concerning the steps which are being taken to correct the problem, the COMMISSION may
suspend funding, permanently terminate this Agreement or revoke the grant.
4. Any deviation or failure to comply with the purpose and/or conditions of this Agreement without prior written
COMMISSION approval may constitute sufficient reason for the COMMISSION to terminate this Agreement,
revoke the grant, require the return of all unspent funds, perform an audit of expended funds, and require
the return of any previously spent funds which are deemed to have been spent in violation of the purpose or
conditions of this grant.
5. This Agreement may be modified only by a written amendment signed by the Executive Director or by persons
authorized by the Executive Director on behalf of the COMMISSION and GRANTEE. Any notice given pursuant to
this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be considered to have been given when actually received by the
following addressee or their agents or employees:

I. In the event of a dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or relating in any way to the Agreement, the
complaining Party shall notify the other Party in writing thereof. Within 30 calendar days of such notice,
representatives of both Parties shall meet at an agreed location to attempt to resolve the dispute in good
faith. Should the dispute not be resolved within 30 calendar days after such notice, the complaining Party
shall seek remedies exclusively through arbitration, in accordance with the provisions of A.R.S. § 12-1501
through 12-1518.
II. The arbitration demand must be a clear and concise statement of the claim or dispute. The respondent's
answer and any counterclaims must be filed within 20 calendar days of service of the demand.
III. The arbitration shall be conducted in Maricopa County.
IV. The arbitration shall be conducted by one arbitrator. If the Parties are not able to agree upon the selection
of an arbitrator, within 20 calendar days of the commencement of an arbitration proceeding by service of a
demand for arbitration, the court on application of a Party shall appoint the arbitrator.
V. The arbitrator must promptly set a conference to clarify the claims and defenses, to establish fair
procedures, and to set a schedule for completing the arbitration.
VI. It is the intent of the parties that, barring extraordinary circumstances, arbitration proceedings will be
concluded with 120 calendar days from the date the arbitrator is appointed. The arbitrator may extend the
time limit in the interests of justice. Failure to adhere to this time limit shall not constitute a basis for
challenging the award.

Contracts signed by County Manager pursuant to Board of Supervisors Resolution: Contract
with Jay Valenzuela for the Northern Arizona Law Enforcement Training Academy as a Recruit
Training Officer and Contract for Professional Services with HDR Engineering, Inc. for
Engineering Consultant, Contract No. B23-02-015, Task 2 Modernization of Engineering
Design Guideline and Standard Details Project
Background:
Independent Contractor will be assigned to the Northern Arizona Law Enforcement Training
Academy (NALETA) as a Recruit Training Officer (RTO): His duties will consist of the
development of new police recruits by coordinating training, coordinating instructors to teach,
filling in as needed for instructors who were not available to instruct, writing AZPOST
approved exams for the recruit class, administering the exams, grading of exams, tracking, and
inputting of results, grading recruits for Northern Pioneer College credits, and forwarding the
grades to Northern Pioneer College for credit. Additionally, responsible for conducting physical
fitness sessions, mentoring and instruction in various law enforcement subjects.

contractor.  Neither party is or shall purport to be an agent, employee, partner, joint

NAVAJO COUNTY PUBLIC WORKS DEPARTMENT 
HOLBROOK, AZ 
 
SCOPE 
For 
NAVAJO COUNTY ENGINEERING CONSULTANT (B 23-02-15) 
TASK 2 – Modernizing of Design Guidelines and Standard Details 
 
HDR Engineering, Inc. 
JULY 7, 2023 
The purpose of this task is t o Modernize the Navajo County’s (NC) Roadway Policy and Design 
Manual (RPDM). HDR will utilize similar Local Government Engineering Design and Construction 
Manual (LGEDCM) as the basis for the new document and will supplement/revise the information to 
incorporate the existing (RPDM) where applicable. Jurisdictions will be used on an as needed or 
recommended basis, such as Maricopa Association of Governments (MAG) and the Arizona 
Department of Transportation (ADOT). 
Maricopa County Association of Governments Standard Specifications and Details for Construction 
will be referred to for specifications and standard details. These documents will not be incorporated 
into the document and will be noted to see the MAG website. AutoCAD files of the standard details 
PDFs will not be provided. The work also excludes the development of standalone specifications, 
standard drawings, and detailed guidelines. 
The County has requested one complete document too include Roadway, Drainage, Traffic, Bridge 
and Geotechnical requirements as applicable. Existing documents, policies and procedures will be 
used when available and will be supplemented with other agencies in Arizona.
 
 
SCOPE OF WORK 
 
Task 1.0 Project Management:  This work includes monitoring the budget, overseeing project 
progress, establishing the project execution timeline, developing and coordinating scope of 
works, and submitting monthly status reports and invoices to the NC Public Works Department 
Project Manager. 
Task 2.0 Meetings:  This work involves attending meetings, provide meetings agendas and 
document meeting minutes. It is anticipated that a total of 3 meetings will be needed for this 
project as detailed in the included estimate. The Kick-Off-Meeting (KOM) will start the project 
and discuss the project approach and timeline. It is assumed all meetings will be conducted 
virtually and no in-person meetings are required. 
Task 3.0 Roadway:  The AASHTO Green Book will be used as the primary reference for Roadway 
Design. Roadway typical sections will also be included in the manual and will be based on the 
current typical sections without any need to show lane expansions or future development.  
Portions of the Coconino County Engineering CADD Manual will be incorporated into the new 
RPDM. 
Landscaping will be minimal in nature and may be adjusted as the document progresses. At 
this time plant types, sizes, rock gradation, etc… are not to be included into the document. 
Task 4.0 Drainage:  HDR will utilize similar LGEDCM as the basis for the new document and will 
supplement/revise the information to incorporate the existing (RPDM) where applicable, as 
developed through the research task.

<!-- page 841 -->
CITY OF PHOENIX STREET TRANSPORTATION DEPARTMENT 
BRIDGE & DAM SAFETY SECTION 
 
 
 
 2 
Task 5.0 Traffic: HDR will utilize similar LGEDCM as the basis for the new document. Only signing 
and pavement marking requirements and guidelines will be provided. Traffic Signals and ITS 
will not be included. Lighting requirements will be per the subdivision guidelines, meet dark sky 
requirements and will be general requirements without specifics on poles and/or materials. 
Roadway classification terminology is to be brought into alignment with AASHTO and other 
agencies terminology. It is assumed all county roadways are tow lane roadways (one-lane in 
each direction) and that one roadway classification would be developed. 
Task 6.0 Bridge:  Per discussions with NC Public Works Department, ADOT sets the standard for 
bridges and miscellaneous structures such as box culverts, pipe and culvert headwalls, 
retaining walls and sound barrier walls.  As such, the work will include referencing ADOT 
Bridge Design Guidelines, ADOT Standard Specifications, ADOT Stored Specifications, ADOT 
Bridge Group Standard Drawings, and other pertinent ADOT references for these structures.  
The work excludes referencing of other agencies. The work also excludes the development of 
specifications, standard drawings, and detailed guidelines. 
Task 7.0 Geotech:  HDR will utilize similar LGEDCM the basis for the new document and will 
focus on providing pavement recommendation for one roadway pavement section. 
Task 8.0 Quality Control/Quality Assurance:  The work will include reviewing the initial and final 
reports for conformity and meeting the task order SOW and objectives. 
Schedule:  This schedule is based on starting work on receipt of notice to proceed (NTP). 
-Initial Design Guideline Submittal for Review: 90 calendar days after NTP  
 
- Final Design Guideline Submittal To NC: 45 calendar days after comments 
(Assumes 14-day review period for NC Public Works Department to provide comments on 
the Initial Submittal)

CSA’s Purpose 
A non-partisan forum for Arizona’s 61 
county supervisors to address important 
issues facing local constituents, providing a 
mechanism to share information and to 
advance a state and federal policy agenda.
CSA’s Core Goals
Protect and enhance county authorities and resources in order to 
promote efficient, responsive constituent services.
Develop and disseminate information to assist state and local    
decision-making.
Empower supervisors and professional staff to influence policy 
decision-makers at the state and federal level.

Select Bills:
Water
Executive Actions
Governor Hobbs establishes Water Policy Council.
• CSA Executive Director Craig Sullivan is one of the 37 individuals appointed 
to the Council.
Basin states reach short-term Colorado River compromise.
• To temporarily stave off federally imposed cuts – either by-right or pro-rata - 
California, Arizona, and Nevada have agreed to conserve 3 million acre-feet 
(MAF) of Colorado River Water over the next three years.
• Using already-approved funding from the Inflation Reduction Act ($5 billion) 
the federal government will compensate users for the voluntary 
conservation of 2.3 MAF. 700,000 acre-feet of voluntary conservation will 
be uncompensated.
Release of new groundwater models.
• Hassayampa Sub-basin Groundwater Model (January 20, 2023).
• Area is west of the White Tank mountains and northwest of Phoenix.
• Over a 100-year period, the Hassayampa sub-basin will see total 
unmet demand of 4.4 MAF.
• Phoenix AMA Groundwater Model (June 2, 2023).
• Phoenix AMA covers 5,646 square miles.
• Over a 100-year period, the Phoenix AMA will see total unmet demand 
of 4.86 MAF.
Legislative Actions
Prioritizing member requests, Legislature earmarked 
nearly half of WIFA’s FY ‘24 monies.
• To get the budget across the finish line, Legislative 
Leadership and Governor Hobbs tapped $143 million from 
the $333 million scheduled for WIFA’s Long-Term Water 
Augmentation Fund in FY 2024.
Legislature expands eligibility for WIFA Water 
Conservation Grant Fund.
• Among other items, expands eligibility for the Water 
Conservation Grant Fund to Arizona’s tribes and private water 
providers.
WIFA Actions
After last year’s massive overhaul of the Authority, 
WIFA begins the grant application process.
• The first round of the Authority’s Water Conservation Grant 
Fund applications closed in late-May. The second round is 
ongoing.

SCR 1006 death benefit; assault; first responders (Gowan)
• Creates the “State Supplemental Benefit Fund,” funded by an additional $20 penalty “on every conviction for a criminal 
offense,” that would be used to provide $250,000 death benefits to the spouse or children of a first responder killed in the 
line of duty. 
SCR 1015 initiative; referendum; signatures; legislative districts (Mesnard)
• Presently, groups seeking to get initiatives and referendums on the ballot are required to get the signatures of 10% and 
5% of the state’s qualified electors, respectively.
• Were SCR 1015 to be approved, groups would have to get identical proportions of signatures from the qualified electors 
of each legislative district. 
HCR 2033 primary elections; eligible candidates (Smith)
• Specifies that direct primary elections for federal, state, county, and city offices must be conducted so that each qualifying 
political party may have candidates equal to the number of open seats at the general election.
HCR 2039 governor; emergency powers (Chaplik)
• Puts a 30-day time limit on the Governor’s emergency powers for each individual emergency. Allows 
longer time frames at the discretion of the Legislature.

Board of Supervisors Regular 5. c.        
Meeting Date: 07/18/2023  
Title: Resolution annex/deannex between Town of Pinetop-Lakeside and City of Show
Low
Submitted By: Melissa Buckley, Clerk of the Board of Supervisors
Department: Board of Supervisors
Presented By: Jason Moore
Motion before the Board:
PUBLIC HEARING: Consideration and Adoption of Resolution Number 22-23, deannexing
territory from the Town of Pinetop-Lakeside and annexing the same territory to the City of
Show Low.
Background:
Pursuant to A.R.S. § 9-471.02, The Town of Pinetop-Lakeside passed and adopted Ordinance
No. 23-463 declaring the de-annexation of the territory. The City of Show Low passed and
adopted Ordinance No. 2023-03 annexing the same territory.
Notice of hearing has been sent to both the Town of Pinetop-Lakeside and the City of Show
Low. 
Requirements of A.R.S. §9-471.02, have been satisfied.  
9-471.02. Deannexation of land from one municipality and annexation to another municipality;
deannexation of right-of-way from a municipality to a county
D. The ordinance passed by each governing body shall be filed with the county board of
supervisors which shall set a hearing date of not less than thirty nor more than sixty days from
the date of the filing of the ordinances and shall notify the governing body of each city or town
of the hearing date at least thirty days prior to the date.
F. On determining that the requirements of this section have been satisfied, on the holding of
the public hearing and on determination that the protests filed are insufficient as defined by this
section, the county board of supervisors shall order that the territory be deannexed from one city
or town and that the same territory be annexed to another city or town as specified in the two
ordinances authorized by this section.
J. A copy of the order of the county board of supervisors ordering the deannexation and
annexation of any land described in any city or town, certified by the clerk of the board, shall be
filed for record in the recorder's office of the county in which the land is situated. The record, or
a copy of the order or decree, certified by the clerk of the board, shall be proof of the
deannexation and annexation of the land.

WHEREAS, pursuant to A.R.S. § 9-471.02, The Town of Pinetop-Lakeside passed and adopted 
Ordinance No.  23-463 declaring the deannexation of the territory described as follows: 
 
Assessor Parcel Numbers: 212-11-102A, 212-11-103A, 212-11-103B, 212-11-102B; Further

That portion of Section 15, Township 9 North, Range 22 East of the Gila and Salt River Base

and the North half of the West half of the West half of the Northeast quarter of the Northwest 
quarter of said Section. 
 
That portion of Section 15, Township 9 North, Range 22 East of the Gila and Salt River Base 
and Meridian, Navajo County, Arizona, more particularly described as follows:  
 
The South half of the East half of the East half of the Northwest quarter of the Northwest quarter 
and the South half of the West half of the West half of the Northeast quarter of the Northwest 
quarter of said Section. 
 
WHEREAS, The City of Show Low passed and adopted Ordinance No. 2023-03 annexing the 
same territory described above; and 
 
WHEREAS, the aforesaid Ordinances were filed with the Navajo County Board of Supervisors; 
and

Low; and 
 
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that a copy of this order be filed with the Recorder’s Office of

Background:
We have received the Healthy People Healthy Communities IGA for over six years and several
of the programs are included in the IGA have been in existence for much longer than that. Prior
to them all being combined into this integrated IGA, they were funded individually.  Some of
these programs offered are child and suicide fatality reviews, our Teen Health Program, and
Tobacco and Chronic Disease Program.  We are able to offer education and skill development to
help our residents improve their quality of life with this funding, as well as identify contributors
that lead to injury, death and poor health outcomes so we can develop and implement
interventions to reduce the risk of these reoccuring..

The Office of Tobacco Prevention and Cessation (“Office of Tobacco”) within the Bureau of Chronic Disease and Health 
Promotion (“BCDHP”) at Arizona Department of Health Services (ADHS) has historically supported evidence- based 
programs and system level changes that assist smokers in disparate or high- risk populations with tobacco prevention 
and cessation services. In Arizona, there are populations that are disproportionately impacted by tobacco use. Currently, 
priority populations identified by the Office of Tobacco are:   1) youth, 2) the justice- involved, and 3) those enrolled in 
the Arizona Healthcare Cost Containment System (AHCCCS). 
 
County health department partners are required to identify three (3) populations that are disproportionately impacted 
by tobacco use in their communities, which may include the three populations identified above or with other populations 
which may be identified based on county-level data. Counties will provide the selected population groups with targeted 
evidence-based programs and activities for two components: 1) Tobacco Prevention and 2) Tobacco Cessation. In 
addition, counties will participate in three ADHS- led work groups that will explore innovative approaches to tobacco 
programming that address 1) Youth; 2) Secondhand Smoke (SHS); and 3) Emerging Issues. Counties will also engage 
in in-person and virtual meetings as identified by ADHS. 
 
The strategies within the Healthy People Healthy Communities (HPHC) Intergovernmental Agreement (IGA) are 
population-based approaches that will require collaboration and support from key community partners, as well as 
promote health system level changes within healthcare systems and employers. These tobacco prevention and 
cessation strategies align with the U.S. Surgeon General’s Report on Smoking Cessation 2020, the Centers for Disease 
Control (CDC) National Comprehensive Tobacco Control Program (NTCP), and Arizona Health Improvement Plan 
(AzHIP) 2021-2025. 
 
The Tobacco component of the HPHC IGA is funded by Proposition 200, which states that tobacco tax dollars under 
the Health Education Account (HEA) requires monies be spent on “programs for the prevention and reduction of tobacco 
use.” Arizona Revised Statute (A.R.S. § 36-772) authorizes four types of expenditures by the HEA: contracts with county 
health departments and other local partners, administrative expenses, advertising, and evaluation of programs. 
Spending these monies for lobbying for political campaigns is expressly prohibited.  
 
The County Contractor must select one (1) or more strategies from this strategic area.  
 
This Exhibit defines the Program Strategy/s within each Strategic Area: 
 
1. Strategic Area: Tobacco 
 
1.1 Reduce tobacco-related disparities among target populations. Counties will select populations based on local 
available data, including tobacco prevalence rates (BRFSS, AYS, YRBSS), CHIP, and CHA data, to inform 
programming; 
 
1.1.1 Prevent the initiation of tobacco use (including emerging products and e-cigarettes) among youth and 
young adults (required), 
 
1.1.1.1 Maintain current peer -to-peer youth programming to empower youth leadership and 
engagement via the Students Taking a New Direction (STAND), the statewide anti-tobacco 
youth coalition; 
 
1.1.1.2 Support the ADHS -selected contractor with recruiting youth participants for statewide 
Enforcement efforts; and

Exhibit C 
 
EVIDENCE-BASED STRATEGIES FOR TEEN PREGNANCY PREVENTION 
 
The Teen Pregnancy Program offers strategic approaches to improve the health and social well-being of youth through 
the reduction of teen pregnancies and sexually transmitted infections/diseases, and the awareness of healthy 
relationships and life skills, including financial literacy and educational and career success.  The program provides youth 
with knowledge and skills that can be applied throughout their lives. Program models are evidence- based, age 
appropriate, medically accurate, and culturally relevant and incorporate a positive youth development approach.  
 
The teen pregnancy prevention programs also offer a Parent/Youth Communication Education component which can 
give parents the tools to actively engage in meaningful communication with their teens on a variety of topics including 
sexual health issues. Parents, grandparents and guardians of a teen are welcome and encouraged to participate in 
these educational sessions.  
 
Proposition 203, The Healthy Arizona Initiative, was passed by Arizona voters in November 1995, authorizing the use 
of lottery funds when available to be utilized for teen pregnancy prevention programs.   The funds from the lottery 
became available in July 2005.  The Arizona Department of Health Services (ADHS), Bureau of Women’s and Children’s 
Health (BWCH), Teen Pregnancy Prevention Program, is charged with the implementation of these funds.    
 
Proposition 207, The Smart and Safe Act, was passed by Arizona voters in November 2020, authorizing the legal use 
of recreational marijuana. The funds from this act will be available on July 1, 2021. The Arizona Department of Health 
Services (ADHS), Bureau of Women’s and Children’s Health (BWCH), is charged with the implementation of a portion 
of these funds. 
 
The County Contractor must select one (1) or more strategies from this strategic area.

Exhibit E 
 
EVIDENCE-BASED STRATEGIES FOR SUICIDE MORTALITY REVIEW 
 
Suicide is preventable. In Arizona, both the number and rate of suicides continues to rise. Arizona’s rate of suicide per 
100,000 people was 24% higher than that of the United States in 2017. In 2018, suicide ranked 8th among the leading 
causes of death but contributed substantially to premature mortality. Pursuant to A.R.S.  § 36-199 and § 36- 199.01, 
ADHS is establishing a Suicide Mortality Review Program in the Arizona Department of Health Services (ADHS) . The 
program will conduct an annual analysis on the incidences and causes of suicides in the state during the preceding 
fiscal year. This analysis will help to inform what changes are needed to decrease the incidence of preventable suicides, 
and as appropriate, take steps to implement these changes. ADHS will fund, encourage and assist in the development 
of local county health department Suicide Mortality Review Teams in their local jurisdiction and to develop suicide 
prevention recommendations for their communities.  
 
On March 3, 2020 Governor Doug Ducey joined mental health advocates, legislators and family members affected by 
suicide to sign Senate Bill 1523, also known as Jake's Law. The bill is named in honor of Jake Machovsky, an Arizona 
teen who lost his life to suicide in 2016 after battling mental health issues. The law requires insurance companies to 
cover mental health treatment and creates the Children's Behavioral Health  Services Fund and provides $8 million for 
behavioral health services for children who are uninsured or underinsured. The law prohibits insurance companies from 
denying coverage for services that are covered by the plan simply because they are delivered in an educational setting. 
This law also establis hes a mental health parity advisory committee to ensure that all parties including families, 
providers, advocacy organizations, and insurers have a voice at the table, creates a suicide mortality review team to 
review deaths by suicide and provide policymakers with improved data and recommendations, and helps increase 
follow-up services for patients at risk for suicide.  
 
Proposition 207, The Smart and Safe Act, was passed by Arizona voters in November 2020, authorizing the legal use 
of recreational marijuana. The funds from this act will be available on July 1, 2021. ADHS, through the Bureau of Chronic 
Disease and Health Promotion , is charged with the implementation of a portion of these funds. The five (5) year IGA 
action plan(s) and activity/activities developed by the local health department will address the following:  
 
1) A.R.S. § 36-199 and § 36-199.01: Suicide Mortality.

Health (NCPHSD)
Background:
This is a long-standing grant between ADHS and Navajo County. This is the new contract for
the 5-year grant cycle.  We are seeking a signature for renewal of the contract.  This contract
provides funding to assist us to perform TB testing for individuals exposed to tuberculosis and to
coordinate follow-up confirmatory testing and evaluation to identify positive cases.  State statute
requires contact tracing and follow-up of all active TB infections, to include Direct Observed

allows for purchase of TB testing supplies, treatment medications, salary/ERE to offset public
health nurse expenses and allowances for training/travel to keep staff abreast of the latest TB
trends and recommendations.  TB is a highly infectious disease and ability to identify and
contain it quickly is essential to ensure the health of the public.

Title: Child Care Health Consultant Multi-Region Grant Renewal FY24
GRA-STATE-24-1245-01
Submitted By: Deborah Huish, Program Manager
Department: NC Public Health Services District
Motion before the Board:
Renewal of the State Government agreement, GRA-STATE-24-1245-01, Child Care Health
Consultation strategy with First Things First, for fiscal year 2024, July, 1 2023, to June 30, 2024
Background:
The Child Care Health Consultation program began first implementing this strategy with the
Navajo County Public Health Services District in February 2014. This is a statewide strategy
that uses certified Child Care Health Consultants who are health professionals, or those with
various degrees which includes health, to work with early care, education administrative and
teaching staff at centers and homes to increase their knowledge and compliance with
best-practice health and safety practices. The Child Care Health Consultation strategy is a
component of the statewide Quality First program model. Quality First provides support to early
care, education, and preschool providers throughout the state of Arizona, that helps to improve
the quality of early learning environments. Child Care Health Consultants work with these
participants who are enrolled in Quality First. This strategy, with the Navajo County Public
Health Services District provides Child Care Health Consultation services within the following
First Things First determined regions: Navajo Nation, Navajo/Apache, San Carlos Apache
Tribe and White Mountain Apache Tribe. Currently services are provided to 42 child care sites,
with the potential to expand to 61 child care centers or homes. When the program was first
implemented here within the Navajo County Public Health Services District, it started with
approximately 25 child care centers and homes, and one employee. Currently, there are two
employees covering these four regions; one servicing the Navajo Nation region, and the other
who is also the Program Manager, servicing the Navajo/Apache, San Carlos Apache Tribe, and
the White Mountain Apache Tribe regions. Examples of some health topics covered by
trainings, or presentations with child care centers/homes, as well as with community members,
have been Handwashing, Disease Transmission, Sanitation, Safe Sleep, Playground Safety, Oral
Health, and Medication Administration.

MEMORANDUM OF AGREEMENT 
1.0 SUPERSEDES: 7/24/2020 
 
2.0 INTRODUCTION 
The purpose of this memorandum is to establish a management agreement between the Navajo County hereinafter 
referred to as the Collaborative Operating Group (COG), and the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) 
IPAWS Program regarding the utilization and security of  Navajo County Interoperable System(s) (as shown in 
Appendix A), which interoperate with the IPAWS-Open Platform for Emergency Networks (IPAWS-OPEN). The 
expected benefit is to enable information interoperability across emergency response organizations and systems as 
intended by the FEMA IPAWS Program.  
This agreement will govern the relationship between the Collaborative Operating Group and FEMA, including 
designated managerial and technical staff and system users associated with the aforementioned COG. As indicated 
within the terms of this agreement, both parties agree to allow system interoperability through the use of SOAP over 
HTTPS via the public internet. Under this agreement, no direct or networked connection using VPN (or equivalent 
technology) between the systems named in Appendix A and IPAWS-OPEN is allowed. In the event a direct 
connection is required, an Interconnection Security Agreement must be executed.  
3.0 AUTHORITY 
This agreement is authorized under the following authorities and regulations:  
 Section 706 of 47 U.S.C. 666, The War Powers Act: Provides for Presidential Access to commercial 
communications during “a state of public peril or disaster or other national emergency”  
 Public Law 93-288, The Stafford Act. Sec. 202. Disaster Warning: Directs FEMA to provide technical 
assistance to State and local governments to ensure that timely and effectively disaster warning is provided 
 Public Law 114-143, The IPAWS Modernization Act: Enacts to law the policy statement and similar 
requirements found in Executive Order 14307 
 Sec. 202. Disaster Warning: Directs FEMA to provide technical assistance to State and local governments to 
ensure that timely and effectively disaster warning is provided 
 Executive Order 13407 of June 26, 2006, Public Alert and Warning System: Established as policy the 
requirement for the United State to have an effective, reliable, integrated, flexible, and comprehensive 
system to alert and warn the American people  
 47 CFR Part 10, Wireless Emergency Alert (WEA): Provide for alert and warning to devices on wireless 
carrier networks 
  47 CFR Part 11, Emergency Alert System (EAS): Provide for alert and warning over TV and radio 
broadcast 
 
4.0 BACKGROUND 
It is the intent of both parties to this agreement to establish and utilize a standardized web based application interface 
(as defined by the IPAWS-OPEN Web Service Interface Design Guidance) between the information technology (IT) 
systems shown below to facilitate the exchange of emergency messages within the production environment.  The 
testing of the interoperability of these systems has been performed through the use of FEMA's Test and Development 
environment to ensure the transference and receipt of emergency messages using approved messaging standards.  The 
interoperability between these systems is supported by the use of SOAP over HTTPS via the public internet.   
5.0 COMMUNICATIONS 
Frequent formal communications are essential to ensure the successful management and operation of system 
interoperability. Both parties agree to maintain open lines of communication between designated staff (as indicated in 
Appendix B) at both the managerial and technical levels. All communications described herein must be condu cted in 
writing and may be disseminated by electronic means unless otherwise noted.  
DocuSign Envelope ID: 4C0C0FA5-CE20-4C1E-817E-914844F3E78F

<!-- page 999 -->

4 
V4.8, April 26, 2022 
The owners of the respective systems agree to designate and provide contact information for technical leads for their 
respective systems, and to facilitate direct contacts between technical leads to support the management and operation 
of system interoperability. To safeguard the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the systems and the data they 
store, process, and transmit, both parties agree to provide notice of specific events within the timeframes indicated 
below:  
 Security Incidents: Technical, administrative and/or help desk staff will immediately notify their designated 
counterparts by telephone or e-mail when a security incident(s) is detected and/or a violation of the Rules of 
Behavior (see Appendix C) has been identified. Both parties agree to make the appropriate technical and 
administrative individuals available for all necessary inquiries and/or investigations. Containment and/or 
resolution procedures will be documented by the identifying party and after-action reports generated and 
submitted to the system owner and/or designated security officials within five (5) business days after detection of 
the incident(s). 
 Disasters and Other Contingencies:  The FEMA IPAWS Program Office will notify the COG by telephone, e-
mail or other acceptable means in the event of a disaster or other contingency that disrupts the normal operation 
of IPAWS-OPEN.  
 System Interconnections: This MOA is intended for systems interoperating with IPAWS-OPEN using SOAP 
over HTTPS via the public Internet.  If in the future, an interconnection (i.e. dedicated system -to-system 
connection) is required to IPAWS-OPEN, this MOA must be updated and an Interconnection Security 
Agreement (ISA) must be executed. If a change in status from interoperating to interconnected system is 
required, the initiating party will notify the other party at least 3 months before the planned interconnection is to 
be in place.  
 Discontinuation of Use: In the event the use of IPAWS-OPEN is no longer required, the COG agrees to 
immediately notify, in writing, the FEMA IPAWS Program Office at which time the COGID and associated 
access credentials will be deactivated. 
 Personnel Changes: Both parties agree to provide notification of changes to their respective system owner or 
technical lead. In addition, both parties will provide notification of any changes in the point of contact 
information provided in Appendix B.  All relevant personnel changes and changes to con tact information must 
be provided within 5 business days of the change. 
6.0 TYPE OF INTERCONNECTIVITY 
Both parties agree that the COG will utilize only the assigned COGID, associated credentials and digital certificates 
provided by the FEMA IPAWS Program Office to support interoperability between the system(s) listed in Appendix 
A and IPAWS-OPEN. In addition, all interoperable systems must be configured to interface with IPAWS -OPEN over 
the public Internet using only approved web service standards and associated requirements.  A listing of approved 
web service standards and supporting requirements can be obtained from the IPAWS-OPEN Web Service Interface 
Design Guidance document.  
In the event, a dedicated connection is required, both parties will agree to negotiate and execute an Interconnection 
Security Agreement (ISA) as required per Department of Homeland Security (DHS) policy which must be signed by 
all required parties before the interconnection is activated. Proposed changes to either system that affect system 
interoperability will be reviewed and evaluated to determine the potential impact. If the proposed changes impact the 
agreed upon terms, the MOA will be renegotiated and executed before changes are implemented.  
7.0 SECURITY 
To ensure the joint security of the systems and the message data they store, process, and transmit, both parties agree 
to adhere to and enforce the Rules of Behavior (as specified in Appendix C).  In addition, both parties agree to the 
following: 
 Ensure authorized users accessing the interoperable system(s) receive, agree to abide by and sign (electronically 
or in paper form) the IPAWS-OPEN Rules of Behavior as specified in Appendix C. Each jurisdiction is 
responsible for keeping the signed Rules of Behavior on file or stored electronically for each system user.

 Utilize FEMA approved PKI certificates to digitally sign messages as they are transported over the public 
Internet. 
 Certify that its respective system is designed, managed and operated in compliance with all relevant federal laws, 
regulations, and policies. 
 Document and maintain jurisdictional and/or system specific security policies and procedures and produce such 
documentation in response to official inquiries and/or requests.   
 Provide physical security and system environmental safeguards for devices supporting system interoperability 
with IPAWS-OPEN.  
 Ensure physical and logical access to the respective systems as well as knowledge of the COGID and associated 
access criteria are only granted to properly vetted and approved entities or individuals.  
 Where applicable, ensure that only individuals who have successfully completed FEMA-required training can 
utilize the interoperable systems to issue alerts and warnings intended for distribution to the public.  
 Where applicable, document and maintain records of successful completion of FEMA -required training and 
produce such documentation in response to official inquiries and/or requests.  
8.0 PROFICIENCY DEMONSTRATION 
Once enabled, each COG operating under this agreement must demonstrate their ability to compose and send a 
message through the IPAWS-OPEN system at regular intervals. Such demonstration must be performed on a monthly 
basis through generation of a message successfully sent through the IPAWS-OPEN Training and Demonstration 
environment.  
9.0 ASSOCIATED SOFTWARE REQUIREMENTS 
The COG will need to select a software package which will allow the COG to properly populate a Common Alerting 
Protocol (CAP) message which complies with both the OASIS Common Alerting Protocol Version 1.2 and the OASIS 
Common Alerting Protocol, v. 1.2 USA Integrated Public Alert and Warning System Profile Version 1.0. With respect 
to the software and the software vendor selected FEMA expects the selected software to provide the following 
minimum critical capabilities and services: 
 Permissions: 
o The ability to assign and manage user permissions; and 
o The ability to retrieve and view IPAWS Alerting Permissions 
 Proficiency: 
o The provision of vendor support, to include user training, and around the clock technical support ; 
and 
o The ability to submit both live and test digital certificates, with clear, easily identifiable information 
that indicates the environment to which the software is pointed (Live or Test)  
 User Interface: 
o The provision of an intuitive user interface, to include help menus; and 
o The ability to notify the user of digital certificate expiration; and 
o The ability to constrain event types and geocodes to user permissions; and 
o The ability to send one alert to multiple channels; and 
o The provision of displays that show required fields based on selected channel; and 
o The ability to pre-populate fields to the greatest extent possible; and 
o The ability to support templates; and 
o The ability to create a polygon or circle, of less than 100 nodes; and

o The ability to update or cancel an alert, without having to reenter all of the data; and 
o The ability to alert the end user if a software license has expired; and 
o Clear explanations if alert information is case sensitive when entered  
 Confirmation and Error Checking: 
o The ability to pre-check an alert message for errors, prior to sending; and 
o The ability to create free-form 90-character WEA text, while preventing prohibited characters; and 
o The provision to IPAWS of alert status codes for any sent alert, with a clear definition of whether 
the codes are advice codes or error codes, along with the meaning of those codes; and 
o The provision of user confirmation of connectivity to IPAWS; and 
o The ability for users to see alert history and/or logs 
10.0 COST CONSIDERATIONS 
This agreement does not authorize financial expenditures by the COG on behalf of FEMA. The FEMA IPAWS 
Program is responsible for the costs associated with developing, operating and maintaining the availability of the 
IPAWS-OPEN system.  The COG is responsible for all costs related to providing their users with access to IPAWS -
OPEN via the public Internet.  These costs may include hardware, software, monthly Internet charges, completion of 
security awareness training and other related jurisdictional costs.  
11.0 PROPERTY OWNERSHIP 
Each Party agrees and acknowledges that nothing in this Agreement shall be construed as giving a party any 
proprietary rights in or to the intellectual property of the other party.  Each Party further agrees that nothing in this 
Agreement shall be construed as creating or granting to a party any implied or exp ress license in or to the intellectual 
property of the other party.  
12.0 TIMELINE 
This agreement will remain in effect based on the life of the Authority to Operate (ATO) for IPAWS -OPEN or a 
maximum of three (3) years after the last date on either signature in the signature block below. Upon expiration of the 
IPAWS-OPEN ATO or after three (3) years (whichever comes first), this agreement will expire without further action 
and system access privileges will be revoked. If the parties wish to extend this agreement , they may do so by 
reviewing, updating, and reauthorizing this agreement. This agreement supersedes all earlier agreements, which 
should be referenced above by title and date. If one or both of the parties wish to terminate this agreement 
prematurely, they may do so upon 30 days' advanced notice or in the event of a security incident that necessitates an 
immediate response. This agreement may be suspended by FEMA for failure to perform the Proficiency 
Demonstration for two consecutive months. A suspended COG may be reinstated upon a completion of a successful 
Proficiency Demonstration.

with the COG and used for interoperating with IPAWS-OPEN.  This Appendix must be amended as applicable systems are

 IPAWS-OPEN 
Function: 
IPAWS-OPEN is the backbone system that structures the alert and distributes the 
message from one interoperating and/or interconnected system (message sender) to 
another interoperating and/or interconnected system (message recipient).

Description of data,

Sensitive Information or classified information. Each message that flows through the 
IPAWS-OPEN system will be associated to a specifically assigned system User ID and 
COGID as captured within the message elements. This information will be retained in 
system logs.

Appendix C 
IPAWS-OPEN Rules of Behavior 
1.0 INTRODUCTION 
The following rules of behavior apply to all persons with application access to Navajo County Interoperable 
System(s) and/or who have been issued a COGID with associated credentials for IPAWS -OPEN.  These individuals 
shall be held accountable for their actions related to the information resources entrusted to them and must comply 
with the following rules or risk losing their access privileges. The Rules of Behavior apply to users on official travel 
as well as at their primary workplace (e.g., Emergency Operations Center – EOC) and at any alternative workplace 
(e.g., telecommuting from a remote or satellite site) using any electronic device including laptop computers and 
portable electronic devices (PED’s).  PED’s include personal digital assistants (PDA’s) (e.g. Palm Pilot s), cell 
phones, text messaging systems (e.g., Blackberry), and plug-in and wireless peripherals that employ removable media 
(e.g. CDs, DVDs, etc.). PEDs also encompass USB flash memory (thumb) drives, external drives, and diskettes.  
These Rules of Behavior are consistent with existing DHS policies and DHS Information Technology (IT) Security 
directives and are intended to enhance the awareness of each user’s responsibilities regarding accessing, storing, 
receiving and/or transmitting information using IPAWS-OPEN. 
2.0 APPLICATION RULES 
2.1 Official Use 
 IPAWS-OPEN is a Federal application to be used only in the performance of the user’s official duties in 
support of public safety as described in the National Incident Management System (NIMS).  
 The use of the IPAWS-OPEN for unauthorized activities is prohibited and could result in verbal or written 
warning, loss of access rights, and/or criminal or civil prosecution. 
 By utilizing IPAWS-OPEN, the user of the interoperable system(s) consents to allow system monit oring to 
ensure appropriate usage for public safety is being observed. 
 Navajo County will be held accountable for safeguarding all configuration items and information entrusted 
to them by FEMA.  Navajo County is expected to manage the relationship with supporting vendors, 
consultants and any other entities providing system support on their behalf.  In addition, Navajo County 
will be held accountable in the event of a security breach or disclosure of sensitive c onfiguration 
information such as digital certificates.  Navajo County understands that the use of digital signatures, used 
on their behalf, is binding and Navajo County will be held accountable accordingly.  In the event sensitive 
information is mishandled, utilization of IPAWS-OPEN may be immediately revoked by FEMA.   
 If software interoperating with IPAWS-OPEN enables users to geo-target public alert messages by means 
of geospatial polygons or circles, then the user shall restrict any such geospatial boun daries so as to remain 
within the geographical limits of their public warning authority (or as near as possible), as determined by 
applicable state and/or local laws and duly adopted operational plans. 
2.2 Access Security 
 All Email addresses provided in connection with interoperable system(s) user accounts must be associated 
to an approved email account assigned by the user’s emergency management organization. The use of 
personal email accounts to support emergency messaging through IPAWS -OPEN is prohibited. 
 Upon approval of the MOA by FEMA, a COG account with COGID and Digital Certificate will be created 
and issued to the designated technical representative.   All individuals with knowledge of these credentials 
must not share or alter these authentication mechanisms without explicit approval from the FEMA IPAWS 
Program. 
DocuSign Envelope ID: 4C0C0FA5-CE20-4C1E-817E-914844F3E78F

<!-- page 1007 -->
FOR OFFICIAL USE ONLY // CONTROLLED UNCLASSIFIED INFORMATION  
 
12 
V4.8, April 26, 2022 
 Every interoperable system user is responsible for remote access security as it relates to their use of 
IPAWS-OPEN and shall abide by these Rules of Behavior. 
2.3 Interoperable System User Accounts and Passwords 
 All users must have a discrete user account ID which cannot be the user’s social security number. To 
protect against unauthorized access, passwords linked to the user ID are used to identify and authenticate 
authorized users. 
 Accounts and passwords shall not be transferred or shared.  The sharing of both a user ID and associated 
password with anyone (including administrators) is prohibited. 
 Accounts and passwords shall be protected from disclosure and writing passwords down or electro nically 
storing them on a medium that is accessible by others is prohibited. 
 The selection of passwords must be complex and shall: 
o Be at least eight characters in length 
o Contain a combination of alphabetic, numeric and special characters 
o Not the same as any of the user’s previous 8 passwords. 
 Passwords shall not contain any dictionary word. 
 Passwords shall not contain any proper noun or the name of any person, pet, child, or fictional character. 
Passwords shall not contain any employee serial number, Social Security number, birth date, phone 
number, or any information that could be readily guessed about the creator of the password.  
 Passwords shall not contain any simple pattern of letters or numbers, such as “qwerty” or “xyz123”.  
 Passwords shall not be any word, noun, or name spelled backwards or with a single digit appended, or with 
a two-digit “year” string, such as 98xyz123.  
 Pass phrases, if used in addition to or instead of passwords, should follow the same guidelines.  
 Passwords shall not be the same as the User ID.

Board of Supervisors Regular 6. b. 1.        
Meeting Date: 07/18/2023  
Title: CPR Fee for service approval
Submitted For: Janelle Linn, Health Director 
Submitted By: Amy Stradling, Department Manager
Department: NC Public Health Services District
Presented By: Janelle Linn & Amy Stradling
Motion before the Board:
Consideration and approval to implement a fee for service for CPR and First Aid certification
and be recognized as a Training Center.
Background:
During our fatality review case review, we identified a trend that CPR was not initiated when
individuals were discovered down or in distress.  Upon further investigation, it was determined
this is often because the family members did not know how to provide CPR.  We also receive
frequent inquiries from the community as to if we offer CPR certification.  They're happy to pay
and have requested we implement this service.  We want to remove that barrier by providing
CPR and First Aid certification courses.  We are requesting approval to charge a fee comparable
to other fire departments, CPR training centers and entities to help sustain this program and the
materials needed to provide the service. With BOS approval, Navajo County Public Health
Services District (NCPHSD) will be a recognized HSI CPR training center.  This will provide
another resource for our community to complete the educational course and, if applicable,
receive their certification cards.  The fee for service is comparable to what fire departments and
training centers charge to offer this education, and will increase options and availability for
community members and businesses seeking CPR certification and training.
Recommendation: 
Recommend approval for Navajo County Public Health Services District to become a
recognized CPR training center.  Recommend approval from the BOS for Navajo County Public
Health Services District to charge a fee for service for courses and certification.  The cost
proposed is as follows:
CPR/First Aid $50
CPR only $25
First Aid only $25
Blood Borne Pathogens $25
BLS $30
Baby Sitting CPR (18 years and under) $20
Baby Sitting First Aid (18 years and under ) $20
Babysitting combo (18 years and under) $40

Board of Supervisors Regular 6. b. 2.        
Meeting Date: 07/18/2023  
Title: IGA between NCPHSD and Coconino County Public Health for Alternative
Medical Examiner Services
Submitted For: Janelle Linn, Health Director 
Submitted By: Rhonda Krouse, Health Division Manager 
Department: NC Public Health Services District Division: Code Enforcement Division
Presented By: Rhonda Krouse
Motion before the Board:
Consideration for approval  of an amendment to the existing Intergovernmental Agreement
between Coconino County Public Health Services District and Navajo County Public Health
Services District for the continued use of the Coconino Public Health Medical Consultant /
Alternative Medical Examiner Services, including a 4% increase for services rendered.
Background:
Navajo County Public Health Services District has partnered with Coconino County Health and
Human Services Medical Examiner’s office for many years.  We utilize their services such as
the post-mortem exams, chart reviews, documentation obtained for the investigation, and any
further additional examinations such as testing, any analysis to assist us in the distinctions
between manners of death.  The reason behind the fee increase is due to inflation and the
increased cost of equipment and resources needed for these services. 
Coconino County has increased the amount for their services by 4%.  This is due to the increase
of inflation and the cost of equipment utilized to perform these specific services.  In the FY
2022-23 budget, physician services was budgeted as $33,000.  Currently, we are at $55,246.60
due to the high volume of deaths in our county that we do not have a way of predicting. As
deaths increase or decrease, so will the budget.  At this time, don't project this increase in price
to put us over budget. 
Recommendation: 
We recommend approval by the Board for the amendment to this IGA to allow the continuous
partnership of services.

 This Intergovernmental Agreement (“Agreement”) is entered into between the Navajo 
County (“County”), a political subdivision of the State of Arizona , and the Coconino County 
Public Health Services District (“Independent Contractor”) (collectively “Parties”).  Both Parties 
are public agencies of the State of Arizona as defined in Arizona Revised Statutes (“A.R.S.”)

follows: 
 
1. Purpose 
 
 The purpose of this Agr eement is to establish the terms and conditions under which 
Independent Contractor  will provide Public Health Medical Consultant/Alternative Medical 
Examiner services.  
 
2. Term 
 
 This Agreement shall commence and be effective upon its execution  beginning July 1, 
2023 and shall be for a period of five (5) years, unless terminated, canceled or extended by either 
Party as provided for in this Agreement.  This Agreement has a cost increase escalator of 4% 
annually starting on July 1 basis, unless terminated or cancelled by either party.  
 
3. Termination 
 
This Agreement may be terminated by either Party upon written notice to the other Party 
given no later than thirty (30) days before the proposed termination date; provided, 
however, that termination shall not b ecome effective until furnishing proper notice to 
the other party, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Parties.

4. Services 
   
 Independent Contractor shall perform the work described below in a competent and 
professional manner to the satisfaction of County.  
  
A. County duties include:  
i. After determining jurisdiction, the County Medico -Legal Death Investigator 
will request a chart review or post-mortem examination from the Independent 
Contractor. 
1) If the County requests a chart review and the Independent Contractor

B. Independent Contractor duties include:

23. Cancellation for Conflict of Interest 
 
 Pursuant to A.R.S. §38-511, either Party may, within three (3) years after the execution of 
this Agreement, cancel it without further penalty or obligation if any person significantly involved 
in initiating, negotiating, securing, drafting, or creating this Agreement is at any time while the 
Agreement is in effect, an employee or agent of any other Party to the Agreement in any capacity 
or a consultant to any other Party, of the contract with respect to the subject matter of the 
Agreement.  A cancellation made pursuant to this provision shall be effective when either Party 
receives written notice of the cancellation unless the notice specifies a later time. 
 
24. Non-discrimination 
 
 The Parties shall comply with Executive Order 2009-09 and all other applicable State and 
Federal employment laws, rules, and regulations, mandating that all persons shall have equa l 
access to employment opportunities, and that no person shall be discriminated against due to race, 
creed, color, religion, sex, national origin or disability. 
 
25. Mutual Indemnification 
 
 Each Party (as “Indemnitor”) agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the other 
Parties (as “Indemnitees”) from and against any and all claims, losses, liability, costs or expenses 
(including reasonable attorney fees), hereinafter collectively referred to as “claims,” arising out of 
bodily injury of any person (including death) or property damage, but only to the extent that such 
claims which result in vicarious/derivative liability to the Indemnitees, are caused by the act, 
omission, negligence, misconduct, or other fault of the Indemnitor, its officers, offici als, agents, 
employees, or volunteers. 
 
26. Entire Agreement 
 
 This Agreement and those documents incorporated by reference represent the entire 
understanding between the parties. No amendment shall be effective unless executed by both 
parties with the same formality as this Agreement. Provided, however, that the County Manager 
is authorized to modify the scope of work as described in Section 1, in writing, with the 
concurrence of Independent Contractor so long as significant additional compensation is not 
required.

Board of Supervisors Regular 7. a.        
Meeting Date: 07/18/2023  
Title: ABAN 23-01: Proposed Abandonment of a Half Cul-De-Sac off Meadow Lane:
District V
Submitted For: Bill Bess, County Engineer/Assistant Public Works Director 
Submitted By: Bryan Cook, Sr. Engineering Project Manager II
Department: Public Works
Presented By: Madhav Mundle
Motion before the Board:
Consideration of Resolution Number 23-2023, granting a Right-of-Way Abandonment of an
un-named partial cul-de-sac adjacent to lots 74, 75, & 76 recorded in plat book 5 page 45. 
Background:
Applicants Jack and Toni Gessner are seeking to abandon a portion of public right-of-way in
District V located west of lots 74 & 75  as identified on the Plat for Rainbow Lake Estates Plat
Book 5 page 45. These lots are also known as APN # 212-32-060A and 212-32-060B and have
been merged into 212-32-060C.  It is the applicants desire to build on the property where the
half cul-de-sac is affecting this action. 
During staff review, it was determined that no parcels would be landlocked, the proposed
abandonment is not being used and does not provide a benefit to the public or has the potential
for county maintenance. It has been determined during the review that for the abandonment, if
approved, the applicants will need to complete the following: 
Hire an Appraiser to determine fair market value for the abandonment. 
Acquire a Quit Claim Deed for the abandonment with appropriate legal description
Obtain a Plat Amendment
Staff sent out notices to property owners within 300' as well as notified utility companies 60
days in advance with directions to contact us if there were concerns, issues, or complaints about
the proposed abandonment. During this timeframe, we received two phone calls for clarification
from the public. Both, once understanding where and what was occurring, did not have any
complaints about the abandonment.  We also received a letter from one of the callers who was
concerned about it being a different and full cull-de-sac used by them. We have attached the
letter and the concern was addressed during the phone call.
In addition, we received a phone call from Arizona Water Company. We notified them that our
abandonment is for public roadways and that underlaying utility usage is not affected and
remains in place. That the applicant would need to work with the utility providers to relocate
any utility usage through granting additional easement and relocating if acceptable by the
utilities.

Staff recommends approval of the abandonment request with the stipulations presented in the

RESOLUTION NO._____-23 
A RESOLUTION OF THE NAVAJO COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS  
GRANTING A RIGHT-OF-WAY ABANDONMENT OF A  
UN-NAMED PARTIAL CUL-DE-SAC ADJACENT TO LOTS 74, 75, & 76  
 RECORDED IN PLAT BOOK 5 PAGE 45 
 
WHEREAS, the Board of Supervisors of Navajo County is authorized by Section 28-6701 and 28-6709 of 
the Arizona Revised Statutes to abandon portion of pubic roadways that are no longer necessary for public use; 
and 
WHEREAS, the Abandonment is for an un-named partial cul-de-sac adjacent to and west of Lots 74 and 
75, east of Lot 76 and north from the edge of ROW for Meadow Street as dedicate in Plat Book 5 page 45;  
WHEREAS, the application has been vetted by Staff and determined that no parcels will be landlocked , 
that the ROW is not needed for public benefit, the portion to be abandoned is not part of Navajo County’s 
Maintenance System and; 
WHEREAS, the application has been reviewed by the Deputy County Attorney and Navajo County has the 
legal capacity and authority to abandon public ROW. 
WHEREAS, the Board of Supervisors, having heard public comment and after due consideration for those 
facts presented; find that with consideration of public safety, health, general welfare and convenience warrant the 
following action; 
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that by the Board of Supervisors of Navajo County; does hereby 
Grant a right-of-way abandonment as stated in this resolution with the following stipulation: 
o The applicant will, at their own expense, retain an appraiser acceptable to Navajo County to 
appraise the abandonment area for fair market value.  
o The applicant will, at their own expense, retain professional services to create a  legal 
description and quit claim deed for the un-named cul-de-sac that is being abandoned.  
o Together with the quit claim deed, legal description, and an agreed upon appraised value will be 
used by the Board of Supervisors to approve the sale of a portion of public roadway  by 
resolution pursuant to ARS § 28-6701, 6709, and 7204. 
o Should the above requirements not be met within one (1) year time from the recording of this 
resolution due to inaction or otherwise loss of interest in proceeding. This resolution will be 
void and the right-of-way will be once again considered as public property.

Board of Supervisors Regular 7. c.        
Meeting Date: 07/18/2023  
Title: Task Agreement No. 34- N8065 Gravel
Submitted For: Madhav Mundle, Public Works Director 
Submitted By: Jeanine Carruthers, Deputy Director Administration
Department: Public Works
Presented By: Madhav Mundle
Motion before the Board:
Consideration of Task Agreement Number 34 to the Intergovernmental Agreement between
the  Bureau of Indian Affairs-Navajo Region and Navajo County that authorizes funding
assistance to provide gravel material on BIA Route 8065 within the Central Agency. 
Background:
The Black Mesa Chapter has been advocating for some years to maintain route 8065 for the
community members who have been facing adversity each year through the inclement weather.
The chapter has been focused on fixing drainage crossings and roadway surfaces to make the
road passable for students and elderly people. Due to the limited funding for the BIA-Chinle
Agency, they have gone forth to request for gravel material to be applied on both sides of the
upcoming drainage crossing. This partnership with Navajo DOT and BIA will plan to gravel an
estimate of 1 mile of roadway. In which County will provide materials, while Navajo DOT and
BIA will provide the workforce to prepare and apply gravel. This Task Agreement will replace
Task Agreement No. 31 which expired on June 30, 2023.
Recommendation: 
Staff recommends Approval of Task Agreement No. 34.
Fiscal Impact
Fiscal Year: FY 2024
Budgeted Y/N: Y
Amount Requested: 100000
Fiscal Impact:
Funds are budgeted under District I Navajo Nation Funds.

RE: GRAVEL PLACEMENT ON N8065 
 
Dear Ms. Benally, 
 
The Chinle Agency Branch of Road Maintenance is requesting for Navajo County’s financial 
assistance for purchasing gravel and the placement of material on BIA Route N8065. The 
monetary assistance and labor to process  gravel material w ould be greatly apprec iated. The 
improvements to roadway would benefit  local travelers traveling during inclement weather 
conditions (snow and rain).  T he improvements have been a reoccurring topic brought to our 
attention, essential for the safety of the traveling community.  But with the limit funding the 
Chinle Agency – Branch of Road Maintenance receives annually.  It’s almost impossible for the 
program to purchase and placement without significantly hindering our annual road maintenance 
budget.  The local communities and our organizations within this area that utilize N8065 would 
greatly appreciate the assistance for this project.  
 
It’s our understanding that Navajo County can make this request possible with funding they 
have obtained.  Again, your assistance  will greatly be appreciated by the surrounding 
communities and other organizations that would greatly benefit from this effort. 
 
Your favorable review and approval are appreciated. 
 
If you have any questions don’t hesitate to contact Mr. Lorenzo Dugi, Chinle Agency - Branch 
of Road Maintenance at Office: 928-674-5176 to personally discuss the specific details of the 
plans and preparations for the event. 
 
 
      Sincerely,
