Title: RAISE grant agreement with the U.S. Department of Transportation for Southern
Navajo County Regional Multimodal Planning Study
Submitted For: Madhav Mundle, Public Works Director 
Submitted By: Kenichi Maruyama, Strategic Initiatives Manager
Department: Public Works
Presented By: Madhav Mundle & Ken
Maruyama
Motion before the Board:
Consideration of accepting a grant award in the amount of $261,000 from FY2022 Rebuilding
American Infrastructure with Sustainability and Equity (RAISE) Grant Program with $29,000
local match and authorizing staff to conduct the Southern Navajo County Regional Multimodal
Planning Study in compliance with the grant's terms and conditions.
Background:
The U.S. Department of Transportation Rebuilding American Infrastructure with Sustainability
and Equity (RAISE) Grant Program provides $2.275 billion in FY 2022 discretionary grant
funding for rail, transit, road and port infrastructure construction projects and planning studies.
RAISE projects are evaluated on eight statutory criteria of 1) safety, 2) environmental
sustainability, 3) quality of life, 4) mobility and community connectivity, 5) economic
competitiveness and opportunity, 6) state of good repair, 7) partnership and collaboration, and 8)
innovation. 
Navajo County was successful in obtaining $261,000 from the RAISE Grant Program for a
planning project that examines the 16-mile segment of SR 260 between US 60 in Show Low to
SR 73 in Pinetop-Lakeside and connecting neighborhoods. It is one of the key multi-modal
planning projects in the 2019 Regional Southern Navajo and Apache County Transportation
Plan for which Navajo County, NACOG, ADOT, the City of Show Low, the Town of
Pinetop-Lakeside, the Town of Taylor, the Town of Snowflake and Apache County comprised
the technical advisory committee.
The project, Southern Navajo County Regional Multimodal Planning Study, will examine areas
for improvement, determine adequate safety measures, and prepare pre?construction
documents. The project will also conduct community outreach, form a technical advisory
committee, and develop a comprehensive plan. The scope of work includes an engineering
study that includes 15% engineering designs roll plots, environmental analysis, related studies
and reports, and construction costs estimates to determine the recommended multi-modal
transportation options for the SR-260 segment between US-60 and SR-73. The project's work
will help the County to apply for additional funds for further design and construction.

<!-- page 1067 -->
Please be advised that the County has secured funding ($29,000) from the Arizona State Match
Advantage for Rural Transportation (AZ SMART) Funds Program to meet the RAISE grant's
local match requirement. Upon the execution of the RAISE grant agreement, the County will
engage in an intergovernmental agreement with Arizona Department of Transportation (ADOT)
for the AZ SMART funding.

Staff recommend approval.

SCHEDULE B 
PROJECT ACTIVITIES 
1. General Project Description. 
This planning project will fund Navajo County’s regional multi‐modal study on the 
approximately 16‐mile segment of SR 260 between US 60 and SR 73 and the 
surrounding neighborhoods. The project will identify areas for improvement, determine 
adequate safety measures, and prepare pre‐construction documents. It will also conduct 
community outreach, form a technical advisory committee, and develop a comprehensive 
plan. 
2. Statement of Work. 
The project’s scope of work will be an engineering study that includes 15% engineering 
designs roll plots, environmental analysis, related studies and reports, and construction 
costs estimates to determine the recommended multi-modal transportation options for the 
SR-260 segment between US-60 and SR-73. 
The work on this study will address the following:  
1. Review the AASHTO Controlling Design Criteria and include the information as an 
appendix to the study. The Final Report may require a justification letter requesting 
Design Exceptions. In addition, the Consultant may be required to prepare a justification 
and request for Design Variances. 
2. Prepare Initial and Final Design Concept Reports (DCR) (including 15% roll plot) that 
are consistent with the short and long-term multi-modal transportation improvement 
plans for SR-260. The documents shall include a detailed analysis and construction cost 
estimates of alternatives being carried forward for evaluation in the DCR.  
3. Prepare Draft and Final Environmental Document and associated technical reports. 
4. Prepare a Traffic Report including detailed evaluations of the potential alternatives. 
Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) will also be evaluated.  
5. Prepare an ADA Compliance and Feasibility Report, as needed.

2. Supporting Narrative. 
As part of the study, consultants will evaluate various transportation demand 
management strategies, including: 
• Arterial Management (the management of traffic signals, dynamic and fixed lane 
management along surface streets including speed management, pedestrian and 
bicycle interaction with vehicles, vehicle priority coordination, and coordination 
with other techniques such as traveler information, electronic payment, or incident 
management).  
• Transit Management (transit service available to a site, personal security, route 
and scheduling information, and coordination with traveler information services.  
• Roadway Operations and Maintenance (the management of work zones and route 
closures through the use of traveler information, lane and speed management 
systems, and enforcement and response service providers).

<!-- page 1080 -->
13 of 18 
• Road Weather Management (planning for and responding to weather events 
impacting traffic operations and roadway conditions, information distribution to 
travelers and response personnel, and operations of facility under inclement 
conditions). 
• Quality Pedestrian Movement (availability of pedestrian facilities that are 
integrated within the overall transportation network and accommodate or even 
promote non-motorized travel). 
These strategies will be applied to the SR-260 corridor to reduce congestion and 
greenhouse gas emissions by optimizing safety and efficiency of the traffic flow, speed 
management, and by promoting non-motorized travel.

Narrative: Luxtiny II– A Mobile Home Community 
LuxTiny II Community is a proposed 3.5 acre Mobile Home community development. Our community is 
part of the small home movement which is a home between 300-750 sq. ft. LuxTiny II is located within in 
a portion of section 25, Township 10 North, Range 21 East of the Gila and Salt River Meridian, city of 
Lakeside, Navajo County, Arizona. The plan envisions an affordable second home or primary residence 
community consisting of mobile homes between 300-750 sq. ft. Located near schools, this will make a 
great location for families and for the retirement community. 
Steve Dedmon, The owner/developer, is a licensed Mobile Home Dealer in the State of Arizona. Our goal 
is to bring in Custom Genesis Homes by Champion into the Community with decks and beautiful outside 
living areas for tenants. 
LuxTiny II will possibly be developed in 3 phases based on Community needs and home availability. Each 
phase will consist of 6 spaces. The subject property is currently undeveloped land. The proposed 
development will meet all the guidelines established in the County’s Development ordinance. 
The proposed project would help local families have a sense of ownership while living in close proximity 
to great schools. This project is planned to start development immediately following the Master Site 
Plan approval. Project will look to finalize all development phases by 2024. 
Thank You, 
Steve Dedmon 
LuxTiny II

GENERAL CHARACTER OF NEIGHBORHOOD:  
 
The majority of the land in the vicinity of this project is zoned A-General, R-3, or C-R, with the north 
and east sides being A -General, the west being C -R, and the south being R -3. A similar, permitted 
manufactured home park, Luxtiny, is located eight hun dred and twenty-five feet (825’) to the south of 
the subject site and is zoned R-3.  
 
BACKGROUND/HISTORY: 
 
The Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission recommends approval of the Zone Change as 
per the June 15th, 2023, hearing with a unanimous vote of 7-0 and a condition by which "the owner of 
the subject property shall begin development within a time perio d. If this development has not begun

schedule for develop ment, or where the property shall be caused to be reverted to its former zoning 
classification" was imposed by Commissioner Booher in his motion to recommend approval.  
 
PROJECT DESCRIPTION:  
 
This project is designed to contain the following components: 
 
- Seventeen (17) one-tenth acre (0.10 ac) spaces for manufactured home placement and resident 
parking 
- All manufactured homes to be placed in the park will be 300-1000 sq. ft. 
- Gravel roads along four (4) sides of the development and three (3) cul-de-sacs, to be built to 
Navajo County standards and able to support at least 75,000 pounds per fire department 
requirements  
 
ZONING DISTRICTS: 
Current:  
ARTICLE  3 – (A-General) – GENERAL ZONING DISTRICT 
 
Section 301 – Purpose  
 
The main purpose of this A-General Zone is to provide for all the unincorporated area of the County, except 
land within the boundary of a reservation and outside the authority of Navajo County not otherwise designated 
for some other specific zone, to be included in the "A-General Zone", by this Ordinance. No subdividing shall 
be conducted or approved in the "A -General Zone", without prior re -zoning of the land so intended. Uses 
permitted in the "A -General Zone", include farm and non -farm residential uses, farms, rec reational, 
institutional, commercial and industrial uses as specifically listed in this Article. Other uses may be permitted 
as Special Uses under Article 20. 
 
Proposed:  
ARTICLE  14 – (R-3) – MULTIPLE-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL ZONING DISTRICT 
 
Section 1401 – Purpose

<!-- page 1157 -->
Board of Supervisors              3 | P a g e  
 
The principal purpose of this zoning district is to provide for multiple -family housing along with certain 
transient residential and non-residential neighborhoods in locations which are suitable and appropriate taking 
into consideration existing conditions, including present use of land, future land use needs and the availability 
of public utilities. The minimum parcel size required is six thousand (6,000) square feet in area and the 
minimum area required for each dwelling unit is one thousand (1,000) square feet. Principal uses permitted in 
this zoning district include high -density housing, hospitals and institutions of an educational, religious, 
charitable or philanthropic nature, private clubs and fraternal organizations, resort hotels, Manufactured home 
subdivisions and Manufactured Home Parks. 
 
ZONING ORDINANCE: 
Article 20 – Special Uses and Planned Unit Developments 
 
Section 2001 – Special Uses 
  
The Board of Supervisors may permit as a Special Use the following uses in zoning districts 
from which they are otherwise prohibited by this Ordinance, unless any such use is further 
prohibited by this Article. 
 
 21. Manufactured Home Parks, subject to all the regulations applicable to Manufactured 
Home Parks as specified in the use regulations for the “R-3” zoning district.

4. SUP 23-004 PINE ROSE MANUFACTURED HOME PARK, DISTRICT IV: Consideration
of a request by Juan Rosales-Perez for a Special Use Permit to allow for
a two phased project, which consists of a 17 space Manufactured Home Park, including 3

Mr. Cody Cooper, Planning Manager, presented the project to the Commission. Mr.
Cooper gave a brief overview of the proposed project, noting a bit of the history of the
property's code violations that have both been opened as well as closed since September
of 2015, and listed the current violations on the site. Mr. Cooper also showed the
Commission some photographs Staff had taken of the site at the time of posting, noting
that there had not been any significant changes. As such, Staff recommended that there be
a condition that all violations be brought into compliance prior to any, and all, permits being
issued to the site. Mr. Cooper then went over the area of notification and presented the list
of the comments against the project, including one petition provided by the neighbors. Mr.
Cooper also noted that the project would fit with the Comprehensive Plan and surrounding
area's characteristics as two similar projects were located to the immediate north and
east.
Mr. Doug Brimhall, a representative of the applicant, approached the Commission to
introduce himself as the Engineer for the project, stating that himself and the applicant
completed additional engineering up front for this project to help satisfy Staff's inquiries,
one of which was how they would access the property. He also stated that the main
ingress/egress would be from Amanda Drive, and that Peterson Drive would be
egress-only and for emergency access.
Commissioner Booher asked if there would be a restriction on the age of the
manufactured homes. Mr. Brimhall said that all homes would be brought up to Navajo
County's Code, but that the applicant had not considered an age restriction.
Mrs. Marilyn Baca, of the public, asked about the size of the parcels. Mr. Brimhall stated
that they would vary in size, ranging from the smallest at 36' x 100', to around 51' x 100'.
The reason for this variation was to accommodate the existing, permitted dwellings.
The Chairman opened for public comments. Mr. Darton Stradling, Mr. Mike Baldwin, and
Ms. Melissa McKinley spoke out against the project. Their complaints are as follows:
    
That Hi Joe Road's access was being used without permission of the property owner.
That there were issues with the easements, that several utility and private easements
were being ignored.
There are flooding issues in the area.
The property was too small to be granted Special Development (SD) for a
Manufactured Home Park.
The density of the project is too great for the area. The property is out of compliance
and a mess.
RV's are illegal to rent in Navajo County.
The trash containment for the site was too close to the neighboring property. That
while the property did have fire hydrants, the flows would not meet the Fire
Department's requirements.
The storage of travel trailers and manufactured homes on the site. The applicant was
making a nuisance of himself to the neighborhood. The age of the manufactured
homes that would be on the property.
 
The Chairman then asked Staff to address these comments.
  
2 of 8 
DRAFT

<!-- page 1164 -->
The Chairman then asked Staff to address these comments.
Mr. Cooper addressed the comments as follows:
    
Amanda Drive is a private ingress-egress that would be the main access to the
project.
Hi Joe Road does not extend to this property, and is not a factor in this application.
The concerns of the easements not being respected is a civil matter and the County
would not be involved in the civil dispute. If the access shown to the County was
found to be insufficient, the applicant would have to either relinquish their Special
Use Permit (SUP) or re-enter the hearing phase as they would have to alter their
plans.
For code violations, having an open violation does not preclude you from pursuing or
obtaining a SUP, which is why Staff is recommending the condition that all violations
be brought into compliance and closed, prior to any permits being issued.
Regarding the concerns of the parcel size, this is not a Special Development project,
this is a SUP and that is not relevant to this project.
Density is not an issue as the Navajo County Comprehensive Plan has encouraged
this area for high density, as there is more access to utilities and services than
outside of the high-density zoning. However, the applicant is required to do a Traffic
Study and make improvements, per the findings of the Traffic Study.
The recent meetings with the Fire Department did not indicate any issues with the
project as well as the project to the east, and Staff is unaware of any changes, as the
plans were given to and approved by the Fire Department, as the applicants have
been working with the Department on this for over a year. However, if the applicant
did need to put in sprinklers, that would be a part of the Building Permit process and
handled in the building phase.
For flooding issues, the applicant is required to have a grading and drainage plan to
follow, and they have provided a preliminary plan for the Commission and the public.
No one is disputing the fact that RV's are illegal to rent in Navajo County, the "RV" in
question would have to be removed prior to development of the project and would not
be allowed in the Manufactured Home spaces.
As far as the trash containment, given that the complainant has stated that it would
be 12 feet from his home, and the building setbacks for the parcels are five feet from
the property lines, this would be an appropriate place for placement of the trash
enclosure.
Commissioner Booher asked for further clarification about the minimum acreage that had
been brought up. Mr. Cooper replied that specific acreage requirement falls under Article
17 for SD Zoning and does not apply to this project as the applicant was not pursuing an
SD Zone Change.
Commissioner Murph asked for more information about the easements. Mr. Cooper said
that it's a public dispute that would have to be handled through the Courts, and Navajo

Commissioner Murph asked if the applicant needed to prove or disprove their access.
Mr. Cooper stated that they were unable to prove or disprove private easements, as they
were outside of the County's purview.
Vice-Chair Smith asked if it was allowed for the Commission to make proving access a

Mr. Steve Dedmon, the applicant, approached the Commission to introduce himself. He

from A-General zoning to the R-3 zoning to allow for more density.
Commissioner Booher asked if there were age restrictions on the homes. Mr. Dedmon
stated that he was now HUD certified and would be building new, custom homes for this
community.
Mrs. Marilyn Baca asked about the ingress and egress, if it was off Hi Joe Road, or if it
would be coming from another road.
Mr. Jeff Rhyan stated that he was also concerned about Hi Joe Road, as it was not County
maintained.
Chairman Latham asked Staff if they would address these comments. Ms. Starke stated
that these comments will be addressed in the next item, but that plans were for the roads to
be brought up to the County standards. Commissioner Smith asked if they would be

6. SUP 23-003 LUXTINY II MANUFACTURED HOME PARK, DISTRICT IV: Consideration
of a request by Steve Dedmon for a Special Use Permit to allow for a 17-space
manufactured home park in Lakeside on a 3.48-acre portion of APN# 212-26-119A,
212-26-119C, 212-26-119D, and 212-26-119E, of T09N, R22E, S24 of the GSRM. Owner: 
Luxtiny LLC. Agent: Steve Dedmon.
Ms. Sondra Starke, Planner I, continued the discussion from the last item and explained
that if the Zone Change was approved, this Special Use Permit would move forward. Ms.
Starke gave the Commission a little more detail about the development and stated that
Staff found it followed the Comprehensive Plan and Zoning Ordinance for the proposed
use already, save that it needed screening. She also noted that the road would have to be
engineered to support the weight of a fully loaded firetruck. (75000 lbs.)
Commissioner Booher asked if Hi Joe Road was a County road or a private road. Mr.
Cody Cooper, Planning Manager, stated that Hi Joe was a private easement and not
maintained by the County.
Mrs. Marilyn Baca asked if the developer could have ingress-egress from Porter Mountain
Road, citing how property owners had been struggling to maintain Hi Joe Road but that
speeding cars typically ruined their efforts. She further stated that she didn't believe the
outlet to Flag Hollow road would be able to handle the increase in traffic the project would
bring.
Chairman Latham asked the applicant to address this question.
Mr. Dedmon stated that he had worked on maintaining his portion of Amanda Road for
their first project, and that he had made an agreement with the neighboring projects to
maintain the road. He also noted that they had started a fund to have Amanda Road paved
in the future, and that they had been working with the County Engineer, Mr. Bill Bess, to
work toward cost estimates. The plan for this project would follow similar steps for
maintenance, if desired by residents. Mr. Dedmon also confirmed that they would be
engineering the road to meet the Fire Department's standards.
Commissioner Booher asked about the maintenance, and if the developer’s tenants
would be involved in maintaining the road. Mr. Dedmon confirmed that the road would be
maintained to the boundary of his development.
Mr. Jeff Rhyan stated that he was under the impression that a road doesn't have to be
paved to be County maintained.
Ms. Starke addressed this, stating that for the County to maintain a road, it needed to meet
a certain level of daily traffic and be brought to that level of maintenance before the County
would adopt the roadway into the maintenance system.
Chairman Latham noted that the developer could also form a road improvement district.
Vice-Chair Smith motioned that the Commission recommend approval of the SUP to the
Board of Supervisors, Commissioner Booher seconded. The motion passed
unanimously, 7 - 0.

7. SUP 23-005 AZ3 PENROD WIRELESS COMMUNICATION FACILITY, DISTRICT IV:
Consideration of a request by State 48 Development Consulting for a Special Use Permit
to allow for the construction of a 110’ monopine wireless communication tower and
associated facility in the Show Low area. APN# 210-01-009F, T10N, 22E, S33 of the
GSRM. Owner: Allen Daniel & Velmarie Foster. Agent: Shannon McCrea.
Mr. Cody Cooper, Planning Manager, presented the item to the Commission. He showed
the Commission some slides of the area, of the style of pole, and some simulated visuals
provided by the applicant. Mr. Cooper noted that the applicants would surpass the
County’s minimum setback requirements at 110%, given the designation of the parcel. Mr.
Cooper also detailed the applicants’ public outreach information, along with how they
addressed the questions the public had about the tower. There were seven letters received
from the public in support of the project and the applicant's representative, Alex Crowe,
was available for questions.
Mr. Buz Essel spoke to the Commission with concerns over the Zoning Ordinance and
asked if there was even a need for the tower. Mr. Essel also asked if Navajo County
required an Environmental Assessment, stating that it was required by federal law. Mr.
Essel also expressed concern that the law was not being followed regarding call logs
proving a need for the tower as they had to be collected over a lengthy period, and that the
height of the tower was not being given a Variance in due process.
Commissioner Booher asked if he represented a group of people. Mr. Essel stated that
he was representing Concerned Citizens for 5G.
Mr. Nick Schmitz addressed the Commission stating that he was in favor of the project as
the service he experienced was terrible, and that property owners had a need for this in his
community. Mr. Schmitz also asked if the tower would have both 4 and 5 G capability, and
what nearby owners could do to boost the service in the meantime.
Mr. Cooper addressed Mr. Essel’s questions, explaining the tower in question was not in a
platted subdivision that the Zoning Ordinance recognized as a residential zone and thus
did not need a Variance for the height. As for the Environmental Assessment, that would
be a requirement of Federal agencies, not the County, and compliance with Federal
requirements was a recommended condition of approval.
Ms. Alex Crowe said that the tower would be both 4 and 5 G, and as for coverage for the
short-term, she stated that Mr. Schmitz's concerns would be brought to the carrier to see if
they could address them for the area.
Commissioner Murph motioned to recommend approval of the Special Use Permit to the
Board of Supervisors; Commissioner Booher seconded. The motion passed
unanimously, 7 - 0.

Narrative: Luxtiny II– A Mobile Home Community 
LuxTiny II Community is a proposed 3.5 acre Mobile Home community development. Our community is 
part of the small home movement which is a home between 300-750 sq. ft. LuxTiny II is located within in 
a portion of section 25, Township 10 North, Range 21 East of the Gila and Salt River Meridian, city of 
Lakeside, Navajo County, Arizona. The plan envisions an affordable second home or primary residence 
community consisting of mobile homes between 300-750 sq. ft. Located near schools, this will make a 
great location for families and for the retirement community. 
Steve Dedmon, The owner/developer, is a licensed Mobile Home Dealer in the State of Arizona. Our goal 
is to bring in Custom Genesis Homes by Champion into the Community with decks and beautiful outside 
living areas for tenants. 
LuxTiny II will possibly be developed in 3 phases based on Community needs and home availability. Each 
phase will consist of 6 spaces. The subject property is currently undeveloped land. The proposed 
development will meet all the guidelines established in the County’s Development ordinance. 
The proposed project would help local families have a sense of ownership while living in close proximity 
to great schools. This project is planned to start development immediately following the Master Site 
Plan approval. Project will look to finalize all development phases by 2024. 
Thank You, 
Steve Dedmon 
LuxTiny II

GENERAL CHARACTER OF NEIGHBORHOOD:  
 
The majority of the land in the vicinity of this project is zoned A-General, R-3, or C-R, with the north 
and east sides being A -General, the west being C -R, and the south being R -3. A similar, permitted 
manufactured home park, Luxtiny, is located eight hun dred and twenty-five feet (825’) to the south of 
the subject site and is zoned R-3.  
 
BACKGROUND/HISTORY: 
 
The Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission recommends approval of the Zone Change as 
per the June 15th, 2023, hearing with a unanimous vote of 7-0 and a condition by which "the owner of 
the subject property shall begin development within a time perio d. If this development has not begun 
within this time frame, the applicant shall be required to re -enter the public hearing process where it 
will be determined whether they be granted an extension, are considered in compliance with the 
schedule for develop ment, or where the property shall be caused to be reverted to its former zoning 
classification" was imposed by Commissioner Booher in his motion to recommend approval.  
 
PROJECT DESCRIPTION:  
 
This project is designed to contain the following components: 
 
- Seventeen (17) one-tenth acre (0.10 ac) spaces for manufactured home placement and resident 
parking 
- All manufactured homes to be placed in the park will be 300-1000 sq. ft. 
- Gravel roads along four (4) sides of the development and three (3) cul-de-sacs, to be built to 
Navajo County standards and able to support at least 75,000 pounds per fire department 
requirements  
 
ZONING DISTRICTS: 
Current:  
ARTICLE  3 – (A-General) – GENERAL ZONING DISTRICT 
 
Section 301 – Purpose  
 
The main purpose of this A-General Zone is to provide for all the unincorporated area of the County, except 
land within the boundary of a reservation and outside the authority of Navajo County not otherwise designated 
for some other specific zone, to be included in the "A-General Zone", by this Ordinance. No subdividing shall 
be conducted or approved in the "A -General Zone", without prior re -zoning of the land so intended. Uses 
permitted in the "A -General Zone", include farm and non -farm residential uses, farms, rec reational, 
institutional, commercial and industrial uses as specifically listed in this Article. Other uses may be permitted 
as Special Uses under Article 20. 
 
Proposed:  
ARTICLE  14 – (R-3) – MULTIPLE-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL ZONING DISTRICT 
 
Section 1401 – Purpose

<!-- page 1249 -->
Board of Supervisors              3 | P a g e  
 
The principal purpose of this zoning district is to provide for multiple -family housing along with certain 
transient residential and non-residential neighborhoods in locations which are suitable and appropriate taking 
into consideration existing conditions, including present use of land, future land use needs and the availability 
of public utilities. The minimum parcel size required is six thousand (6,000) square feet in area and the 
minimum area required for each dwelling unit is one thousand (1,000) square feet. Principal uses permitted in 
this zoning district include high -density housing, hospitals and institutions of an educational, religious, 
charitable or philanthropic nature, private clubs and fraternal organizations, resort hotels, Manufactured home 
subdivisions and Manufactured Home Parks. 
 
ZONING ORDINANCE: 
Article 20 – Special Uses and Planned Unit Developments 
 
Section 2001 – Special Uses 
  
The Board of Supervisors may permit as a Special Use the following uses in zoning districts 
from which they are otherwise prohibited by this Ordinance, unless any such use is further 
prohibited by this Article. 
 
 21. Manufactured Home Parks, subject to all the regulations applicable to Manufactured 
Home Parks as specified in the use regulations for the “R-3” zoning district.

Goal 4:  Provide equal opportunity for safe, decent, sanitary, and affordable housing for all

Essel also expressed concern that the law was not being followed regarding call logs
proving a need for the tower as they had to be collected over a lengthy period, and that the
height of the tower was not being given a Variance in due process.
Commissioner Booher asked if he represented a group of people. Mr. Essel stated that
he was representing Concerned Citizens for 5G.
Mr. Nick Schmitz addressed the Commission stating that he was in favor of the project as
the service he experienced was terrible, and that property owners had a need for this in his
community. Mr. Schmitz also asked if the tower would have both 4 and 5 G capability, and
what nearby owners could do to boost the service in the meantime.
Mr. Cooper addressed Mr. Essel’s questions, explaining the tower in question was not in a
platted subdivision that the Zoning Ordinance recognized as a residential zone and thus
did not need a Variance for the height. As for the Environmental Assessment, that would
be a requirement of Federal agencies, not the County, and compliance with Federal
requirements was a recommended condition of approval.
Ms. Alex Crowe said that the tower would be both 4 and 5 G, and as for coverage for the
short-term, she stated that Mr. Schmitz's concerns would be brought to the carrier to see if
they could address them for the area.
Commissioner Murph motioned to recommend approval of the Special Use Permit to the
Board of Supervisors; Commissioner Booher seconded. The motion passed
unanimously, 7 - 0.

agenda, or any other topic; and the Commission may direct staff to study or provide
additional information on topics of the Commissions’ choosing.

REQUEST DESCRIPTION:  
A request for a Special Use Permit to construct a two-phased project, which consists of a Manufactured 
Home Park and fourplex on a vacant, 2.83-acre parcel, in the Lakeside area. 
 
GENERAL CHARACTER OF NEIGHBORHOOD:  
 
To the north of this property is an already -constructed Recreational Vehicle Park.  To the east of this 
property is an approved Manufactured Home Park, which has not yet completed construction.  To the 
south and west of the subject property are single-family residences.

BACKGROUND/HISTORY: 
 
The subject property has had a number of Code Enforcement complaints opened, dating back to 
September of 2015.  A number of these complaints have been closed over the years, while a number of 
new complaints have been received and opened for the property. 
 
On-site, there are still open violations related to construction debris, litter (including tires, scrap wood, 
auto parts, broken concrete and masonry blocks), and inoperable vehicles, which have been visible on 
the property occasionally.  There have also b een construction vehicles , such as tractors,  and trailers 
visible on the property on occasion.  These violations fall under Section 2516 – Unsightly, Unsanitary 
or Hazardous Accumulations and Conditions, within the Navajo County Zoning Ordinance. 
 
There are currently three (3) manufactured homes on the property.  Records indicate that two of these 
manufactured homes are permitted and connected to utilities, while the third is not.  This third home 
was on a property that was combined with others to f orm the subject property.  As the third 
manufactured home does not have a permit and is not connected to utilities, it is considered a stored 
manufactured home for Zoning Ordinance purposes.  This manufactured home meets all requirements 
of Section 2514 of the Navajo County Zoning Ordinance regarding the storage of such a structure.  This 
structure will not be able to receive permitting as a dwelling unless the subject site is approved as a 
Manufactured Home Park or is sited on another property, while also following Building Division 
requirements. 
 
At the Thursday, June 15th, 2023 Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission Hearing, the Navajo 
County Planning and Zoning Commission recommended approval of this item by a vote of 6 -1 
(Commissioner Booher), subject to the conditions recommended by Staff. 
 
PROJECT DESCRIPTION:  
 
The proposed project is two-phased, consisting of a Manufactured Home Park and a four-plex apartment 
building. 
 
During Phase I, the applicant is proposing the development of  a Manufactured Home Park, which will 
consist of seventeen (17) total spaces.  Of these spaces, fourteen (14) will be for manufactured homes, 
while three (3) will be for Recreational Vehicles. 
 
Access for Phase I of this project is proposed off of Amanda Drive.  Interior to the property, the owner 
will construct a twenty-five foot (25’) wide gravel roadway, providing access to Lots 1 -14 in the park.  
South of Lot 14, there will be four (4) guest parking spaces. 
 
Additionally, south of Lot 14, there will be a driveway, which will provide access to the RV lots (Lots 
15-17).  This driveway will lead to a trash enclosure, which will allow for the disposal and removal of 
waste from the site. 
 
The roadway for this Manufactured Home Park will extend to the south of the property toward Peterson 
Road.  On the south of the property, there will be a crash gate constructed that will allow residents and 
emergency services to utilize this access to Peterson Road, though only for emergency purposes. 
 
During Phase II of the project, the applicant has indicated that they will convert and renovate an existing

building on site into a building with four (4) apartments.  Accompanying surfaces for this building will 
be required to be ADA compliant.  The apartment building will have its own access from Amanda Drive 
and include a dumpster and trash enclosure. 
 
ZONING DISTRICTS: 
ARTICLE 14 – (R-3) MULTIPLE-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL ZONING DISTRICT 
 
Section 1401 – Purpose.  
 
The principal purpose of this zoning district is to provide for multiple-family housing along with certain 
transient residential and non-residential neighborhoods in locations which are suitable and appropriate 
taking into consideration existing conditions, including present use of land, future land use needs and 
the availability of public utilities.  The minimum parcel size required is six thousand (6,000) square feet 
in area and the minimum area required for each dwelling unit is one thousand (1,000) square feet.  
Principal uses permitted in this zoning district inclu de high-density housing, hospitals and institutions 
of an educational, religious, charitable or philanthropic nature, private clubs and fraternal organizations, 
resort hotels, Manufactured home subdivisions and Manufactured Home Parks. 
 
ZONING ORDINANCE: 
Article 20 – Special Uses and Planned Unit Developments 
 
Section 2001 – Special Uses 
  
The Board of Supervisors may permit as a Special Use the following uses in zoning districts 
from which they are otherwise prohibited by this Ordinance, unless any such use is further 
prohibited by this Article. 
 
21. Manufactured Home Parks, subject to all the regulations applicable to Manufactured 
Home Parks as specified in the use regulations for the “R-3” zoning district.

RESOLUTION ____-23 
 
A RESOLUTION OF THE NAVAJO COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS APPROVING 
A SPECIAL USE PERMIT FOR PINE ROSE MANUFACTURED HOME PARK 
 
WHEREAS, an application for a Special Use Pe rmit was duly filed on April 24, 2023 
by Juan Rosales-Perez to allow for the construction of a two -phased project, which consists of a 
Manufactured Home Park and a fourplex on a vacant, 2.83-acre parcel, in the Lakeside area; and 
 
WHEREAS, the application concerns the foll owing real p roperty in Navajo County: 
APN # 212-26-082N, Township 09 North, Range 22 East, Section 24 of the Gila and Salt River 
Base and Meridian; and 
 
WHEREAS, the application was considered by the Navajo County Planning & Zoning 
Commission at a duly noticed public hearing on June 15, 2023; and 
 
WHEREAS, the Navajo County Bo ard of Supervisors after considering the testimony 
and other evidence presented at t he hearing, as well as the recommendations of Staff, found that 
the Special Use Permit is consistent with the public health, safety and general welfare and should 
be approved subject to the conditions set forth herein; and 
 
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT R ESOLVED the Board of Superviso rs hereby 
approves the Special Use Permit, subject to the following conditions: 
 
Phase 1 
 
1. The applicant shall obtain any require d Navajo County permits, including but not 
limited to building, grading, drainage, and sign permits. 
 
2. All open Code Enforcement complaints shall be closed prior to any permitting or 
construction on-site. 
 
3. No building or structure shall be occupied prior to  compliance with all appropriate 
Building Division requirements. 
 
4. All lighting on the property shall be shielded to reflect downward, be motion -
activated, and be in conformance with the Navajo County Lighting Ordinance. 
 
5. A solid wall or fence, or suitable planting, at least three and one -half feet (3 ½’)  
feet in height, shall be required around the entire boundary of this Special Use site.

<!-- page 1318 -->
Navajo County - For Official Use Only 
 
6. No parking shall be allowed on driveways. 
 
7. The location of Manufactured Homes on designated Recreational Vehicle space s 
shall be prohibited. 
 
8. All trash collection areas shall be enclosed with a fence or wall, as approved the 
County Health Department, to adequately screen the area. 
 
9. Access to Peterson Road through this development shall only be utilized for  egress 
and emergency purposes. 
 
10. A Drainage Study, which meets the Navajo County Drainage Policy, shall be 
submitted and approved. 
 
11. A Grading and Drainage Plan shall be submitted and approved  by Navajo County 
Public Works prior to the issuance of a building permit for any  of the proposed 
structures. 
 
12. A Traffic Study shall be submitted to Navajo County Public Works prior to the 
issuance of a building permit for any of the proposed structures. 
 
13. A Geotechnical Report for gravel roadway section shall be submitted and 
approved. 
 
14. All roads and parking areas are privately maintained roadways and shall include 
Amanda Drive, as well as any internal roads.  The maintenance of these roads and  
parking areas shall be the responsibility of the owner of the subject property.   
 
15. The Fire District shall approve the fire suppression design for the development. 
 
16. The permitted Special Use shall be allowed to occur per the attached/approved site 
plan.  Any expansion or change of the Special Use shall require an amendment to 
this permit. 
 
17. If the permitted Special Use is not utilized within a twelve (12) month period, from 
the date of Board approval, this permit shall become null and void. 
 
18. This Special Use Permit shall be personal to the permittee and applicable only to the 
specific use and to the specific property for which it is issued. Upon completion and fi nal 
inspection by the Planning and Development Services Director (or designee) of any 
authorized structures, signifying that all zoning and site development requirements 
imposed in connection  with the permit have been satisfied, the Special Use Permit shal l 
thereafter be transferable and shall run with the land, whereupon the maintenance of 
special conditions imposed by the permit, as well as the compliance with other provisions 
of this title, shall be the responsibility of the property owner.

<!-- page 1319 -->
Navajo County - For Official Use Only 
 
19. This Special Use Permit and the subject site shall be reviewed and inspected by Planning 
and Development Staff on the fifth (5 th) anniversary of Board of Supervisors approval 
and every five (5) years thereafter to ensure the site is being utilized as approved and is in 
compliance with all conditions contained herein.  If the subject site is found to be out of 
compliance with these conditions, this Special Use Permit and its privileges may be 
revoked. 
 
Phase 2 
 
1. An amended Drainage Study, which meets the Navajo County Drainage Policy, 
shall be submitted and approved. 
 
2. An amended Grading and Drainage Plan shall be submitted and approved  by 
Public Works prior to the issuance of a building permit for any of the  proposed 
structures. 
 
3. The amended Grading and Drainage Plan shall show a hard -pavement surface and 
access to the multiple-family building, in accordance with Americans with 
Disabilities Act (ADA) accessible parking requirements. 
 
4. All trash collection area s shall be enclosed with a fence or wall, as approved the 
County Health Department, to adequately screen the area.

4. SUP 23-004 PINE ROSE MANUFACTURED HOME PARK, DISTRICT IV: Consideration
of a request by Juan Rosales-Perez for a Special Use Permit to allow for
a two phased project, which consists of a 17 space Manufactured Home Park, including 3
Recreational Vehicle spaces, and fourplex on a 2.83-acre parcel in the Lakeside area.
APN# 212-26-082N, T09N, R22E, S24 of the GSRM. Owner: Juan Rosales-Perez. Agent: 
Juan Rosales-Perez.
Mr. Cody Cooper, Planning Manager, presented the project to the Commission. Mr.
Cooper gave a brief overview of the proposed project, noting a bit of the history of the
property's code violations that have both been opened as well as closed since September
of 2015, and listed the current violations on the site. Mr. Cooper also showed the
Commission some photographs Staff had taken of the site at the time of posting, noting
that there had not been any significant changes. As such, Staff recommended that there be
a condition that all violations be brought into compliance prior to any, and all, permits being
issued to the site. Mr. Cooper then went over the area of notification and presented the list
of the comments against the project, including one petition provided by the neighbors. Mr.
Cooper also noted that the project would fit with the Comprehensive Plan and surrounding
area's characteristics as two similar projects were located to the immediate north and
east.
Mr. Doug Brimhall, a representative of the applicant, approached the Commission to
introduce himself as the Engineer for the project, stating that himself and the applicant
completed additional engineering up front for this project to help satisfy Staff's inquiries,
one of which was how they would access the property. He also stated that the main
ingress/egress would be from Amanda Drive, and that Peterson Drive would be
egress-only and for emergency access.
Commissioner Booher asked if there would be a restriction on the age of the
manufactured homes. Mr. Brimhall said that all homes would be brought up to Navajo
County's Code, but that the applicant had not considered an age restriction.
Mrs. Marilyn Baca, of the public, asked about the size of the parcels. Mr. Brimhall stated
that they would vary in size, ranging from the smallest at 36' x 100', to around 51' x 100'.
The reason for this variation was to accommodate the existing, permitted dwellings.
The Chairman opened for public comments. Mr. Darton Stradling, Mr. Mike Baldwin, and
Ms. Melissa McKinley spoke out against the project. Their complaints are as follows:
    
That Hi Joe Road's access was being used without permission of the property owner.
That there were issues with the easements, that several utility and private easements
were being ignored.
There are flooding issues in the area.
The property was too small to be granted Special Development (SD) for a
Manufactured Home Park.
The density of the project is too great for the area. The property is out of compliance
and a mess.
RV's are illegal to rent in Navajo County.
The trash containment for the site was too close to the neighboring property. That
while the property did have fire hydrants, the flows would not meet the Fire
Department's requirements.
The storage of travel trailers and manufactured homes on the site. The applicant was
making a nuisance of himself to the neighborhood. The age of the manufactured
homes that would be on the property.
 
The Chairman then asked Staff to address these comments.
  
2 of 8 
DRAFT

<!-- page 1323 -->
The Chairman then asked Staff to address these comments.
Mr. Cooper addressed the comments as follows:
    
Amanda Drive is a private ingress-egress that would be the main access to the
project.
Hi Joe Road does not extend to this property, and is not a factor in this application.
The concerns of the easements not being respected is a civil matter and the County
would not be involved in the civil dispute. If the access shown to the County was
found to be insufficient, the applicant would have to either relinquish their Special
Use Permit (SUP) or re-enter the hearing phase as they would have to alter their
plans.
For code violations, having an open violation does not preclude you from pursuing or
obtaining a SUP, which is why Staff is recommending the condition that all violations
be brought into compliance and closed, prior to any permits being issued.
Regarding the concerns of the parcel size, this is not a Special Development project,
this is a SUP and that is not relevant to this project.
Density is not an issue as the Navajo County Comprehensive Plan has encouraged
this area for high density, as there is more access to utilities and services than
outside of the high-density zoning. However, the applicant is required to do a Traffic
Study and make improvements, per the findings of the Traffic Study.
The recent meetings with the Fire Department did not indicate any issues with the
project as well as the project to the east, and Staff is unaware of any changes, as the
plans were given to and approved by the Fire Department, as the applicants have
been working with the Department on this for over a year. However, if the applicant
did need to put in sprinklers, that would be a part of the Building Permit process and
handled in the building phase.
For flooding issues, the applicant is required to have a grading and drainage plan to
follow, and they have provided a preliminary plan for the Commission and the public.
No one is disputing the fact that RV's are illegal to rent in Navajo County, the "RV" in
question would have to be removed prior to development of the project and would not
be allowed in the Manufactured Home spaces.
As far as the trash containment, given that the complainant has stated that it would
be 12 feet from his home, and the building setbacks for the parcels are five feet from
the property lines, this would be an appropriate place for placement of the trash
enclosure.
Commissioner Booher asked for further clarification about the minimum acreage that had
been brought up. Mr. Cooper replied that specific acreage requirement falls under Article
17 for SD Zoning and does not apply to this project as the applicant was not pursuing an
SD Zone Change.
Commissioner Murph asked for more information about the easements. Mr. Cooper said
that it's a public dispute that would have to be handled through the Courts, and Navajo
County did not have the authority to be involved in such a dispute.
Commissioner Murph asked if the applicant needed to prove or disprove their access.
Mr. Cooper stated that they were unable to prove or disprove private easements, as they
were outside of the County's purview.
Vice-Chair Smith asked if it was allowed for the Commission to make proving access a
stipulation or condition, to which Mr. Cooper said they could require that as a part of their
SUP's stipulations or conditions.
Chairman Latham asked if the SUP was approved, if the applicant would have to come

5. ZC 23-001 LUXTINY II MANUFACTURED HOME PARK, DISTRICT IV: Consideration of
a request by Steve Dedmon for a Zone Change from A-General to R-3 to allow for a

212-26-119A, 212-26-119C, 212-26-119D, and 212-26-119E, of T09N, R22E, S24 of the

Ms. Sondra Starke, Planner I, presented the item to the Commission, stating that this item
and the next were linked, but that only the Zone Change was being discussed for this item.
Ms. Starke gave a brief overview of the area's features and showed the Commission a site
plan of the proposed Park, as well as a zoning map showing the Commission the area's
zoning profile. Ms. Starke noted that there is R-3 zoning touching the border of the
property, so there was no concern regarding spot zoning. Additionally, the use fit the
Comprehensive Plan and the surrounding area. Staff received one public comment against
the project that covered several issues, including the development of Hi Joe Road, light
pollution, and urbanization.
Mr. Steve Dedmon, the applicant, approached the Commission to introduce himself. He
currently owns Luxtiny, which is to the south of this project. The applicant wished to change
from A-General zoning to the R-3 zoning to allow for more density.
Commissioner Booher asked if there were age restrictions on the homes. Mr. Dedmon
stated that he was now HUD certified and would be building new, custom homes for this
community.
Mrs. Marilyn Baca asked about the ingress and egress, if it was off Hi Joe Road, or if it
would be coming from another road.
Mr. Jeff Rhyan stated that he was also concerned about Hi Joe Road, as it was not County
maintained.
Chairman Latham asked Staff if they would address these comments. Ms. Starke stated
that these comments will be addressed in the next item, but that plans were for the roads to
be brought up to the County standards. Commissioner Smith asked if they would be
County maintained, to which Staff confirmed that they would not.

6. SUP 23-003 LUXTINY II MANUFACTURED HOME PARK, DISTRICT IV: Consideration
of a request by Steve Dedmon for a Special Use Permit to allow for a 17-space
manufactured home park in Lakeside on a 3.48-acre portion of APN# 212-26-119A,
212-26-119C, 212-26-119D, and 212-26-119E, of T09N, R22E, S24 of the GSRM. Owner: 
Luxtiny LLC. Agent: Steve Dedmon.
Ms. Sondra Starke, Planner I, continued the discussion from the last item and explained
that if the Zone Change was approved, this Special Use Permit would move forward. Ms.
Starke gave the Commission a little more detail about the development and stated that
Staff found it followed the Comprehensive Plan and Zoning Ordinance for the proposed
use already, save that it needed screening. She also noted that the road would have to be
engineered to support the weight of a fully loaded firetruck. (75000 lbs.)
Commissioner Booher asked if Hi Joe Road was a County road or a private road. Mr.
Cody Cooper, Planning Manager, stated that Hi Joe was a private easement and not
maintained by the County.
Mrs. Marilyn Baca asked if the developer could have ingress-egress from Porter Mountain
Road, citing how property owners had been struggling to maintain Hi Joe Road but that
speeding cars typically ruined their efforts. She further stated that she didn't believe the
outlet to Flag Hollow road would be able to handle the increase in traffic the project would
bring.
Chairman Latham asked the applicant to address this question.
Mr. Dedmon stated that he had worked on maintaining his portion of Amanda Road for
their first project, and that he had made an agreement with the neighboring projects to
maintain the road. He also noted that they had started a fund to have Amanda Road paved
in the future, and that they had been working with the County Engineer, Mr. Bill Bess, to
work toward cost estimates. The plan for this project would follow similar steps for
maintenance, if desired by residents. Mr. Dedmon also confirmed that they would be
engineering the road to meet the Fire Department's standards.
Commissioner Booher asked about the maintenance, and if the developer’s tenants
would be involved in maintaining the road. Mr. Dedmon confirmed that the road would be
maintained to the boundary of his development.
Mr. Jeff Rhyan stated that he was under the impression that a road doesn't have to be
paved to be County maintained.
Ms. Starke addressed this, stating that for the County to maintain a road, it needed to meet
a certain level of daily traffic and be brought to that level of maintenance before the County
would adopt the roadway into the maintenance system.
Chairman Latham noted that the developer could also form a road improvement district.
Vice-Chair Smith motioned that the Commission recommend approval of the SUP to the
Board of Supervisors, Commissioner Booher seconded. The motion passed
unanimously, 7 - 0.

7. SUP 23-005 AZ3 PENROD WIRELESS COMMUNICATION FACILITY, DISTRICT IV:
Consideration of a request by State 48 Development Consulting for a Special Use Permit
to allow for the construction of a 110’ monopine wireless communication tower and
associated facility in the Show Low area. APN# 210-01-009F, T10N, 22E, S33 of the
GSRM. Owner: Allen Daniel & Velmarie Foster. Agent: Shannon McCrea.
Mr. Cody Cooper, Planning Manager, presented the item to the Commission. He showed
the Commission some slides of the area, of the style of pole, and some simulated visuals
provided by the applicant. Mr. Cooper noted that the applicants would surpass the
County’s minimum setback requirements at 110%, given the designation of the parcel. Mr.
Cooper also detailed the applicants’ public outreach information, along with how they
addressed the questions the public had about the tower. There were seven letters received
from the public in support of the project and the applicant's representative, Alex Crowe,
was available for questions.
Mr. Buz Essel spoke to the Commission with concerns over the Zoning Ordinance and
asked if there was even a need for the tower. Mr. Essel also asked if Navajo County
required an Environmental Assessment, stating that it was required by federal law. Mr.
Essel also expressed concern that the law was not being followed regarding call logs
proving a need for the tower as they had to be collected over a lengthy period, and that the
height of the tower was not being given a Variance in due process.
Commissioner Booher asked if he represented a group of people. Mr. Essel stated that
he was representing Concerned Citizens for 5G.
Mr. Nick Schmitz addressed the Commission stating that he was in favor of the project as
the service he experienced was terrible, and that property owners had a need for this in his
community. Mr. Schmitz also asked if the tower would have both 4 and 5 G capability, and
what nearby owners could do to boost the service in the meantime.
Mr. Cooper addressed Mr. Essel’s questions, explaining the tower in question was not in a
platted subdivision that the Zoning Ordinance recognized as a residential zone and thus
did not need a Variance for the height. As for the Environmental Assessment, that would
be a requirement of Federal agencies, not the County, and compliance with Federal
requirements was a recommended condition of approval.
Ms. Alex Crowe said that the tower would be both 4 and 5 G, and as for coverage for the
short-term, she stated that Mr. Schmitz's concerns would be brought to the carrier to see if
they could address them for the area.
Commissioner Murph motioned to recommend approval of the Special Use Permit to the
Board of Supervisors; Commissioner Booher seconded. The motion passed
unanimously, 7 - 0.

Background:
The applicant is requesting a Special Use Permit to allow for the construction of a 110’
monopine wireless communication tower and associated facility on a vacant, 7.63-acre parcel, in
the Show Low area.

REQUEST DESCRIPTION:  
A request for a Special Use Permit to allow for the construction of a 110’ monopine  wireless 
communication tower and associated facility on a vacant, 7.63-acre parcel, in the Show Low area. 
 
GENERAL CHARACTER OF NEIGHBORHOOD:  
 
To the north and east of this property is single -family, agricultural land.  To the south and west of this 
property are single-family residences within subdivisions. 
 
BACKGROUND/HISTORY:

<!-- page 1400 -->
Board of Supervisors              2 | P a g e  
 
At the Thursday, June 15th, 2023 Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission Hearing, the Navajo 
County Planning and Zoning Commission unanimously recommended approval of this item, subject to 
the conditions recommended by Staff. 
 
PROJECT DESCRIPTION:  
 
The proposed project is a 110’ monopine  wireless communication tower and its associated facilities.  
This tower will be located at least 121’ feet away from all property lines on APN # 210 -01-009F.  The 
tower and all associated equipment will be located in a 40’ x 40’ area and surrounded by a 10’ tall chain 
link fence. 
 
ZONING DISTRICTS: 
ARTICLE 3 – (A-GENERAL) – GENERAL ZONING DISTRICT 
 
Section 301 – Purpose.  
 
The main purpose of this A -General Zone is to provide for all the unincorporated area of the 
County, except land within the boundary of a reservation and outside the authority of Navajo 
County not otherwise designated for some other specific zone, to be included in the “A-General 
Zone,” without prior re-zoning of the land so intended.  Uses permitted in the “A-General Zone,” 
include farm and non -farm residential uses, farms, recreational, institutional, commercial and 
industrial uses as specifically listed in this Article.  Other uses may be permitted as Special Uses 
under Article 20. 
 
ZONING ORDINANCE: 
Article 20 – Special Uses and Planned Unit Developments 
 
Section 2001 – Special Uses 
  
The Board of Supervisors may permit as a Special Use the following uses in zoning districts 
from which they are otherwise prohibited by this Ordinance, unless any such use is f urther 
prohibited by this Article. 
 
34. Television, wireless towers, and radio transmitter towers and stations, subject to 
approval by Federal Regulatory Agencies. 
 
COMPREHENSIVE PLAN/AREA PLAN:  
Comprehensive Plan 
 
Land Use Element 
 
Goal 6: Maintain compatible land use patterns while encouraging development. 
 
 Policy 6 -B: Consider, if needed, providing for buffers between different land uses

 including, but not limited to, setbacks, walls or fences, and landscaping. 
 
▪ The applicant has indicated that they will setback their wireless communication 
tower a minimum of 121’ from all property lines, which is in excess of the 
requirements of the Navajo County Zoning Ordinance for facilities of this nature.  
They have also indicated a monopine design with the intent of helping the facility 
to blend in with the surrounding environment. 
 
 Goal 9: Actively plan to accommodate growth in Navajo County in an appropriate manner. 
 
Policy 9-F: Encourage development/installation of technology improvements including, 
but not limited to, high speed Internet lines and other communications improvements in 
Navajo County. 
 
▪ The applicant is proposing the addition of this wireless communication tower and 
associated facilities in order to provide higher  quality wireless service for 
residents, businesses, visitors, and emergency services in this region of Navajo 
County. 
 
Analysis: 
 
This project meets all relevant goals and policies of the Navajo County Comprehensive Plan.  The 
Comprehensive Plan encourages buffers that include greater setbacks, which this project provides via 
setbacks that are 110% of the height of the tower.  Communications improvements are also encouraged, 
which this project states it is aiming to provide. 
 
This project, and its submitta l, meet all of the requirements of Section 2521 of the Navajo County 
Zoning Ordinance, which regulates wireless communication facilities.  
 
As of July 5th, 2023, Planning and Development Services Staff have received seven (7) letters that are 
in favor of this Special Use Permit proposal.

PLANNING AND ZONING COMMISSION/STAFF RECOMMENDATION:  
 
The Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission and Navajo County Planning and Development 
Services Staff recommend approval of the Special Use Permit, subject to the following conditions: 
 
1. This Special Use Permit shall permit 1 (one) monopole wireless communication tower, not to 
exceed 110 feet in height, and acc essory structures necessary for the operation of the tower on 
the subject property. 
 
2. The applicant shall obtain a Building Permit from Navajo County for such tower and facilities 
prior to commencing construction. 
 
3. The applicant shall meet all State and Federal requirements concerning communication towers 
prior to any building permits being issued.

<!-- page 1403 -->
Board of Supervisors              5 | P a g e  
 
 
4. The tower shall be constructed as a monopole, as indicated in the supplied plans.  The owner of 
the tower shall maintain the tower, antennae as necessary. 
 
5. A fence of material acceptable to the Planning and Development Services Director shall be constructed 
to enclose the base of the tower and necessary accessory structures.  
 
6. A Geotechnical Report for the Access Easement shall be submitted and approved. 
 
7. The permitted Special Use shall be allowed to occur per the attached/approved site plan.  Any 
expansion or change of the Special Use shall require an amendment to this permit. 
 
8. If the permitted Special Use is not utilized within a twelve (12) month period,  from the date of 
Board approval, this permit shall become null and void. 
 
9. Should the operator decide to abandon the use of the tower, they shall notify Navajo County 
Planning and Development Services that the tower is no longer being utilized. 
 
10. If the tower is no longer being utilized, the property owner shall cause, at their expense, the 
removal of all components of this tower within a 90-day period. 
 
11. The owner shall provide reasonable cooperation to other public and private users who may be 
interested in collocation on this tower and shall consider such collocation upon commercially 
reasonable terms, unless such collocation is not technically feasible. 
 
12. This Special Use Permit shall be personal to the permittee and applicable only to the specific use a nd 
to the specific property for which it is issued. Upon completion and final inspection by the Planning 
and Development Services Director (or designee) of any authorized structures, signifying that all 
zoning and site development requirements imposed in connection with the permit have been satisfied, 
the Special Use Permit shall thereafter be transferable and shall run with the land, whereupon the 
maintenance of special conditions imposed by the permit, as well as the compliance with other 
provisions of this title, shall be the responsibility of the property owner. 
 
13. This Special Use Permit and the subject site shall be reviewed and inspected by Planning and 
Development Staff on the fifth (5 th) anniversary of Board of Supervisors approval and every five (5) 
years thereafter to ensure the site is being utilized as approved and is in compliance with all conditions 
contained herein.  If the subject site is found to be out of compliance with these conditions, this Special 
Use Permit and its privileges may be revoked.

a condition that all violations be brought into compliance prior to any, and all, permits being
issued to the site. Mr. Cooper then went over the area of notification and presented the list
of the comments against the project, including one petition provided by the neighbors. Mr.

Mr. Doug Brimhall, a representative of the applicant, approached the Commission to

egress-only and for emergency access.

Mrs. Marilyn Baca, of the public, asked about the size of the parcels. Mr. Brimhall stated
that they would vary in size, ranging from the smallest at 36' x 100', to around 51' x 100'.
The reason for this variation was to accommodate the existing, permitted dwellings.
The Chairman opened for public comments. Mr. Darton Stradling, Mr. Mike Baldwin, and

That Hi Joe Road's access was being used without permission of the property owner.
That there were issues with the easements, that several utility and private easements

The property was too small to be granted Special Development (SD) for a

The density of the project is too great for the area. The property is out of compliance

RV's are illegal to rent in Navajo County.
The trash containment for the site was too close to the neighboring property. That
while the property did have fire hydrants, the flows would not meet the Fire

The storage of travel trailers and manufactured homes on the site. The applicant was

homes that would be on the property.
 
The Chairman then asked Staff to address these comments.

The Chairman then asked Staff to address these comments.
Mr. Cooper addressed the comments as follows:
    
Amanda Drive is a private ingress-egress that would be the main access to the
project.
Hi Joe Road does not extend to this property, and is not a factor in this application.
The concerns of the easements not being respected is a civil matter and the County
would not be involved in the civil dispute. If the access shown to the County was
found to be insufficient, the applicant would have to either relinquish their Special
Use Permit (SUP) or re-enter the hearing phase as they would have to alter their
plans.
For code violations, having an open violation does not preclude you from pursuing or
obtaining a SUP, which is why Staff is recommending the condition that all violations
be brought into compliance and closed, prior to any permits being issued.
Regarding the concerns of the parcel size, this is not a Special Development project,
this is a SUP and that is not relevant to this project.
Density is not an issue as the Navajo County Comprehensive Plan has encouraged
this area for high density, as there is more access to utilities and services than
outside of the high-density zoning. However, the applicant is required to do a Traffic
Study and make improvements, per the findings of the Traffic Study.
The recent meetings with the Fire Department did not indicate any issues with the
project as well as the project to the east, and Staff is unaware of any changes, as the
plans were given to and approved by the Fire Department, as the applicants have
been working with the Department on this for over a year. However, if the applicant
did need to put in sprinklers, that would be a part of the Building Permit process and
handled in the building phase.
For flooding issues, the applicant is required to have a grading and drainage plan to
follow, and they have provided a preliminary plan for the Commission and the public.
No one is disputing the fact that RV's are illegal to rent in Navajo County, the "RV" in
question would have to be removed prior to development of the project and would not
be allowed in the Manufactured Home spaces.
As far as the trash containment, given that the complainant has stated that it would
be 12 feet from his home, and the building setbacks for the parcels are five feet from
the property lines, this would be an appropriate place for placement of the trash
enclosure.

5. ZC 23-001 LUXTINY II MANUFACTURED HOME PARK, DISTRICT IV: Consideration of
a request by Steve Dedmon for a Zone Change from A-General to R-3 to allow for a
17-space manufactured home park in Lakeside on a 3.48-acre portion of APN#
212-26-119A, 212-26-119C, 212-26-119D, and 212-26-119E, of T09N, R22E, S24 of the
GSRM. Owner: Luxtiny LLC. Agent: Steve Dedmon.
Ms. Sondra Starke, Planner I, presented the item to the Commission, stating that this item
and the next were linked, but that only the Zone Change was being discussed for this item.
Ms. Starke gave a brief overview of the area's features and showed the Commission a site
plan of the proposed Park, as well as a zoning map showing the Commission the area's
zoning profile. Ms. Starke noted that there is R-3 zoning touching the border of the
property, so there was no concern regarding spot zoning. Additionally, the use fit the
Comprehensive Plan and the surrounding area. Staff received one public comment against
the project that covered several issues, including the development of Hi Joe Road, light
pollution, and urbanization.
Mr. Steve Dedmon, the applicant, approached the Commission to introduce himself. He
currently owns Luxtiny, which is to the south of this project. The applicant wished to change
from A-General zoning to the R-3 zoning to allow for more density.
Commissioner Booher asked if there were age restrictions on the homes. Mr. Dedmon
stated that he was now HUD certified and would be building new, custom homes for this
community.
Mrs. Marilyn Baca asked about the ingress and egress, if it was off Hi Joe Road, or if it
would be coming from another road.
Mr. Jeff Rhyan stated that he was also concerned about Hi Joe Road, as it was not County
maintained.
Chairman Latham asked Staff if they would address these comments. Ms. Starke stated
that these comments will be addressed in the next item, but that plans were for the roads to
be brought up to the County standards. Commissioner Smith asked if they would be
County maintained, to which Staff confirmed that they would not.
Commissioner Booher motioned to recommend approval of the Zone Change to the
Board of Supervisors, but that there be a condition that the development be given a time

Board of Supervisors, but that there be a condition that the development be given a time
limit to begin development. Commissioner Muder seconded the motion. The motion
passed unanimously, 7 - 0.
 
6. SUP 23-003 LUXTINY II MANUFACTURED HOME PARK, DISTRICT IV: Consideration
of a request by Steve Dedmon for a Special Use Permit to allow for a 17-space
manufactured home park in Lakeside on a 3.48-acre portion of APN# 212-26-119A,
212-26-119C, 212-26-119D, and 212-26-119E, of T09N, R22E, S24 of the GSRM. Owner: 
Luxtiny LLC. Agent: Steve Dedmon.
Ms. Sondra Starke, Planner I, continued the discussion from the last item and explained
that if the Zone Change was approved, this Special Use Permit would move forward. Ms.
Starke gave the Commission a little more detail about the development and stated that
Staff found it followed the Comprehensive Plan and Zoning Ordinance for the proposed
use already, save that it needed screening. She also noted that the road would have to be
engineered to support the weight of a fully loaded firetruck. (75000 lbs.)
Commissioner Booher asked if Hi Joe Road was a County road or a private road. Mr.
Cody Cooper, Planning Manager, stated that Hi Joe was a private easement and not
maintained by the County.
Mrs. Marilyn Baca asked if the developer could have ingress-egress from Porter Mountain
Road, citing how property owners had been struggling to maintain Hi Joe Road but that
speeding cars typically ruined their efforts. She further stated that she didn't believe the
outlet to Flag Hollow road would be able to handle the increase in traffic the project would
bring.
Chairman Latham asked the applicant to address this question.
Mr. Dedmon stated that he had worked on maintaining his portion of Amanda Road for
their first project, and that he had made an agreement with the neighboring projects to
maintain the road. He also noted that they had started a fund to have Amanda Road paved
in the future, and that they had been working with the County Engineer, Mr. Bill Bess, to
work toward cost estimates. The plan for this project would follow similar steps for
maintenance, if desired by residents. Mr. Dedmon also confirmed that they would be
engineering the road to meet the Fire Department's standards.
Commissioner Booher asked about the maintenance, and if the developer’s tenants
would be involved in maintaining the road. Mr. Dedmon confirmed that the road would be
maintained to the boundary of his development.
Mr. Jeff Rhyan stated that he was under the impression that a road doesn't have to be
paved to be County maintained.
Ms. Starke addressed this, stating that for the County to maintain a road, it needed to meet
a certain level of daily traffic and be brought to that level of maintenance before the County
would adopt the roadway into the maintenance system.
Chairman Latham noted that the developer could also form a road improvement district.
Vice-Chair Smith motioned that the Commission recommend approval of the SUP to the
Board of Supervisors, Commissioner Booher seconded. The motion passed
unanimously, 7 - 0.

7. SUP 23-005 AZ3 PENROD WIRELESS COMMUNICATION FACILITY, DISTRICT IV:
Consideration of a request by State 48 Development Consulting for a Special Use Permit
to allow for the construction of a 110’ monopine wireless communication tower and
associated facility in the Show Low area. APN# 210-01-009F, T10N, 22E, S33 of the
GSRM. Owner: Allen Daniel & Velmarie Foster. Agent: Shannon McCrea.
Mr. Cody Cooper, Planning Manager, presented the item to the Commission. He showed
the Commission some slides of the area, of the style of pole, and some simulated visuals
provided by the applicant. Mr. Cooper noted that the applicants would surpass the
County’s minimum setback requirements at 110%, given the designation of the parcel. Mr.
Cooper also detailed the applicants’ public outreach information, along with how they
addressed the questions the public had about the tower. There were seven letters received
from the public in support of the project and the applicant's representative, Alex Crowe,
was available for questions.
Mr. Buz Essel spoke to the Commission with concerns over the Zoning Ordinance and
asked if there was even a need for the tower. Mr. Essel also asked if Navajo County
required an Environmental Assessment, stating that it was required by federal law. Mr.
Essel also expressed concern that the law was not being followed regarding call logs
proving a need for the tower as they had to be collected over a lengthy period, and that the
height of the tower was not being given a Variance in due process.
Commissioner Booher asked if he represented a group of people. Mr. Essel stated that
he was representing Concerned Citizens for 5G.
Mr. Nick Schmitz addressed the Commission stating that he was in favor of the project as
the service he experienced was terrible, and that property owners had a need for this in his
community. Mr. Schmitz also asked if the tower would have both 4 and 5 G capability, and
what nearby owners could do to boost the service in the meantime.
Mr. Cooper addressed Mr. Essel’s questions, explaining the tower in question was not in a
platted subdivision that the Zoning Ordinance recognized as a residential zone and thus
did not need a Variance for the height. As for the Environmental Assessment, that would
be a requirement of Federal agencies, not the County, and compliance with Federal
requirements was a recommended condition of approval.
Ms. Alex Crowe said that the tower would be both 4 and 5 G, and as for coverage for the
short-term, she stated that Mr. Schmitz's concerns would be brought to the carrier to see if
they could address them for the area.
Commissioner Murph motioned to recommend approval of the Special Use Permit to the
Board of Supervisors; Commissioner Booher seconded. The motion passed
unanimously, 7 - 0.
